blocks: 6.0 PROCEDURE
6.3.1 Position the generator on the north pad. Chock the wheels.
6.3.2 Bond the frame to the ground bar.
6.3.3 Verify the MTS is in the OFF (centre) position.
6.3.4 Open utility breaker CB-1 and apply the station lock.

6.3.5 Land the cables at the generator connection cabinet. Check phase rotation with the
      rotation meter.
6.3.6 Start the generator. Allow 5 min warm-up at no load.
6.3.7 Move the MTS to GENERATOR.
6.3.8 Start pump 1, then pump 2 after 60 s.
6.3.9 Confirm discharge pressure of 68 to 74 psi.
6.3.10 Report "PS-17 pumping on generator" and the time to the Water Incident Lead.
6.4 Running on Generator Power

6.4.1 Record the pumping start time against the dispatch time. The planned hookup and start-up
      time is 150 min (Attachment A); report any overrun and its cause to Logistics.
6.4.2 Log fuel, load and discharge pressure every 4 h on F-WDS-207.
6.4.3 Request fuel at the threshold in WDS 03.322 section 6.3.
6.5 Return to Grid Supply

6.5.1 Return only on the Water Incident Lead's order, after Distribution Operations confirms
      FDR-AIK-2207 is stable.
6.5.2 Stop pump 2, then pump 1.
6.5.3 Move the MTS to OFF, then to UTILITY. Close CB-1.
6.5.4 Restart the pumps on grid power. Run the generator unloaded for 5 min, then stop it.
6.5.5 Leave the generator connected for 12 h if more weather is forecast.
7.0 RECORDS
F-WDS-207 Generator Run Log; F-MAL-022 dispatch request. Retain 5 years.

blocks: 1.0 PURPOSE

This procedure sets how Logistics dispatches portable generators and delivers diesel to SGW
standby and portable generators during declared events.
2.0 SCOPE

Applies to water pump stations, lift stations, tanks with powered controls, and electric
facilities that run on generator power. Does not apply to customer-owned generators, including
hospital standby units such as GEN-HSP-TALLOWBRANCH.
3.0 RESPONSIBILITIES
Logistics Section Chief: owns the fuel plan, vendor call-outs and the generator dispatch log.

Fuel Coordinator (Logistics): receives F-MAL-022 requests, chooses the fuel source, tracks each
delivery to completion.

Water Incident Lead: sets generator priority among water facilities and requests portable
generators. Depot Supervisor, DEP-AIK-GRANITEVILLE: loads FTK-WREN-3 and readies
MGEN-HALBERD-500 for transport.
6.0 PROCEDURE
6.1 Requests
6.1.1 Generator dispatch and fuel requests are made on form F-MAL-022 and logged by Logistics.

6.1.2 The requester gives facility id, generator id, gauge reading, time of reading and load
      (kW).
6.1.3 Fuel Coordinator computes remaining run time from Attachment A.
6.2 Generator dispatch
6.2.1 Water Incident Lead confirms the target site and the connection point per WDS 03.318.
6.2.2 Depot Supervisor starts load-out and reports departure time to Logistics.
6.2.3 Logistics logs dispatched, on-site and running times against the F-MAL-022 number.
6.2.4 NOTE: Hookup and start-up times are set by WDS 03.318 section 6.4, not by this procedure.
6.3 Fuel source selection
6.3.1 Compare the vendor delivery time with the generator's remaining run time.

6.3.2 Where the vendor delivery time is longer than a generator's remaining run time, the SGW
      fuel truck is used first.

6.3.3 Call Altamaha for the next delivery to the same site at the same time, so the truck can be
      released.

6.3.4 Where two sites compete for FTK-WREN-3, the Water Incident Lead sets the order. Sites
      serving a hospital or critical facility per DOM 14.140 go first.
6.3.5 CAUTION: Do not fuel a running generator unless the unit is rated for hot refuelling.
6.4 Records of delivery
6.4.1 Driver records gallons delivered, gauge before and after, and time (24-hour EDT).
6.4.2 Vendor delivery tickets are scanned to the F-MAL-022 record within 12 h.

blocks: 2.0 SCOPE

It applies to diesel standby generators at SGW booster and pump stations in South Carolina and
Georgia. Covered units include GEN-PS38-COPPERLEAF and GEN-PS52-DEERWATER; the full list is in
Attachment A.

It does not apply to portable generators. For PS-17 see WDS 03.318; for monthly load tests see
WDS 03.350.
3.0 RESPONSIBILITIES
Water Incident Lead: approves refuel priority when several stations need fuel at once.
Station Operator: reads and logs fuel level, raises refuel requests.
Water SCADA Operator: watches remote tank-level signals and alerts the Station Operator.
Logistics Section Chief: assigns the vendor or the SGW fuel truck per MAL 05.040.
6.0 PROCEDURE
6.1 Start of Run

6.1.1 When a unit starts on loss of grid supply, record the start time and fuel level on
      F-WDS-207.
6.1.2 Report the start to the Water Incident Lead.
6.1.3 Calculate run time remaining using the Attachment A burn rate.
6.2 Monitoring
6.2.1 Read and log the fuel level every 4 h on F-WDS-207 while the generator runs.

6.2.2 Read the sight gauge, not only the SCADA signal. Record both if they differ by more than 5
      percent.
6.2.3 Log load (kW), oil pressure and coolant temperature with each fuel reading.

NOTE: At unmanned stations a roving operator may cover up to three stations. Keep the 4 h
      interval.
6.3 Refuel Request
6.3.1 When the fuel tank falls to 60 percent, raise a refuel request.

6.3.2 Submit the request on F-MAL-022 to the Logistics desk. State unit id, level, burn rate and
      route.

6.3.3 Flag any route that crosses a low-water crossing in GEP 2F.01 Attachment 2. Copperleaf
      Road (PS-38) and Deerwater Spur (PS-52) are on that list.

6.3.4 If run time remaining is shorter than the vendor delivery time, tell Logistics. Logistics
      then sends the SGW fuel truck first (MAL 05.040).
6.3.5 Log the delivery time and gallons received.
6.4 Shutdown
6.4.1 After return to grid supply, run unloaded for 5 min, then stop.
6.4.2 Top off to 95 percent within 24 h.

6.1 Automatic start on loss of grid supply
6.1.1 Confirm on SCADA that the ATS transferred within 15 s of utility loss.
6.1.2 Confirm pumps 1 and 2 restarted on the lead-lag sequence. Allow 45 s stagger.
6.1.3 Log start time, kW and fuel level on F-WDS-207.

6.1.4 Notify the Water Incident Lead by phone. During business hours also notify the Richmond
      district supervisor.
6.1.5 Dispatch the Station Operator to site within 2 h to verify local readings.
6.2 Run-time monitoring

6.2.1 Read the fuel gauge and log kW, coolant temperature and oil pressure every 4 h on
      F-WDS-207.
6.2.2 Raise the refuel request at the tank level set in WDS 03.322. Use F-MAL-022.

6.2.3 Compare remaining run time against vendor delivery time. If remaining run time is shorter,
      ask Logistics for the SGW fuel truck first (MAL 05.040).
6.2.4 Record any alarm, shutdown or restart with the time in 24-hour format.
6.3 Failure of automatic transfer
NOTE: Use this subsection only on the Water Incident Lead's order.

6.3.2 Place the ATS controller in OFF.
6.3.3 Operate the manual bypass handle to EMERGENCY. Observe the position flag.
6.3.4 Start pump 1 locally. Wait 60 s. Start pump 2.
6.3.5 Report the manual transfer to the Water Control Room Operator and log it.
6.4 Return to grid supply

blocks: 4.0 DEFINITIONS AND ABBREVIATIONS
Service connection: the point where the customer service line meets the SGW main.
Heavy flow: fire flow, main flushing or a main break draining the zone.
Low-pressure event: any verified reading below the state minimum in 5.1 or 5.2.
5.0 PRECAUTIONS AND LIMITS

5.1 South Carolina systems: minimum 25 psi at service connections in normal operation, and 20
    psi under heavy flow (SC R.61-58.7.E(7)).
5.2 Georgia systems: minimum 20 psi at all times (Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. 391-3-5-.10).

5.3 The SCADA low-pressure alarm is set at 40 psi at every zone critical point. Do not lower it
    without Water Incident Lead approval.
5.4 The high-pressure alarm is 110 psi. Above 120 psi, isolate the PRV station.

5.5 A SCADA reading alone is not a verified low-pressure event. Confirm it with a field gauge or
    a second sensor.
7.0 RECORDS

SCADA alarm history (kept 3 years by the historian). Field readings on F-WDS-212. Retain 5
years.
8.0 REFERENCES

SC R.61-58.7.E(7); Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. 391-3-5-.10 WQC 07.114; WQC 07.120; WDS 03.240; WDS

blocks: 6.0 PROCEDURE
6.1 High level (H)
6.1.1 Confirm the filling pump station has stopped on its level control.
6.1.2 If pumps are still running, stop the lead pump from SCADA.
6.1.3 Log the event in the control room log.
6.2 High-high level (HH)
6.2.1 Stop all pumps filling the tank.
6.2.2 Dispatch a Distribution Field Operator to check the altitude valve.
6.2.3 If the altitude valve is stuck open, close the tank inlet valve by hand.
6.3 Overflow
6.3.1 Confirm overflow by camera or field report.
6.3.2 Stop filling. Close the inlet valve.
6.3.3 Estimate the volume lost from the level trend and the overflow pipe size.
6.3.4 Notify the Water Compliance Officer. Report any erosion or off-site flow.
6.3.5 Inspect the overflow screen and flap gate before the tank returns to service.
6.4 Low level (L) and low-low level (LL)
6.4.1 Check whether the filling station is in alarm or without power.

6.4.2 If the filling station has lost power, start tank drawdown tracking per WDS 03.240.
      Drawdown is tracked every 15 min.
6.4.3 At LL, inform the Water Incident Lead. Pressure response follows WDS 03.105.
6.4.4 Do not isolate the tank without the Water Incident Lead's order.
6.5 Before a forecast storm

6.5.1 From 48 h before forecast tropical-storm-force winds, raise each tank to between H and HH
      less 0.5 ft.
6.5.2 Check that the overflow screen is in place and the flap gate closes.
7.0 RECORDS
Control room log; SCADA trend exports kept 3 years. Valve isolations are recorded on F-WDS-212.
8.0 REFERENCES
WDS 03.105; WDS 03.240; WDS 03.115; WQC 07.150 (for tank drains reaching a sewer).

      reaches the residual-pressure limit.

6.1.2 Track the drawdown every 15 min. Report level, rate and time to limit to the Water
      Incident Lead.
6.1.3 If the rate exceeds the Attachment A planning rate by 25 percent, look for a main break.
6.1.4 Ask Communications for a voluntary conservation message for the zone (PCN 02.050).
6.2 Isolation
6.2.1 Propose the segment to isolate, with valve numbers, to the Water Incident Lead.
6.2.2 On the order, record the order time and the ordering position on F-WDS-212.
6.2.3 Operate valves in the listed sequence. Record turns and time per valve.
6.2.4 Report "segment isolated" and the customer count affected.
6.3 Hospital Supply
6.3.1 A potable-water tanker to a hospital needs 120 min from request to connection.
6.3.2 Request the tanker when time to limit is less than 120 min plus 30 min margin.

6.3.3 For Tallow Branch hospital (HSP-AIK-TALLOWBRANCH), connect at the fire-department
      connection on the east dock.
6.3.4 Sample the tanker for free chlorine before connection; minimum 0.2 mg/L.
6.4 Restoration
6.4.1 Open valves only on the Water Incident Lead's order, recorded on F-WDS-212.
6.4.2 Refill the tank before returning the zone to normal pressure settings.
6.4.3 Flush per WDS 03.420 where pressure fell below the floor.
7.0 RECORDS
F-WDS-212 Valve Operation Record; SCADA tank trend. Retain 5 years.

6.0 PROCEDURE
6.1 Alarm
6.1.1 Acknowledge the alarm within 5 min.
6.1.2 Check station status, tank level and any active main break in the zone.
6.1.3 Trend the zone critical point for the past 2 h.
6.2 Field Verification
6.2.1 Send the on-call crew with a calibrated gauge.
6.2.2 Read at the hydrant nearest the critical point. Record the reading, time and hydrant id.
6.2.3 For zones fed by a booster on generator power, read at the station discharge too.
6.3 Restore Pressure
6.3.1 Start standby pumps if available.

6.3.2 If the station has lost power, follow WDS 03.322 (fixed generator) or WDS 03.318 (PS-17
      portable hookup).
6.3.3 Track tank drawdown per WDS 03.240.
6.3.4 Notify critical customers in the zone using DOM 14.140.
6.4 Below the State Minimum

6.4.1 When pressure at a service connection falls below the state minimum, notify the Water
      Compliance Officer within 1 h.

6.4.2 The Water Compliance Officer starts the boil water evaluation under WQC 07.114 (Georgia)
      or WQC 07.120 (South Carolina).

6.4.3 Record the affected streets and zones on the advisory map. Use the zone ids from
      Attachment A.
6.4.4 Keep reading the critical point every 30 min until pressure is above the minimum for 2 h.

CAUTION: Do not start flushing before the boil water decision is made. Flushing can pull
         pressure lower.
6.4.5 Hand the readings to the Water Compliance Officer for the regulator report.

blocks: 1.0 PURPOSE

This procedure sets the triage, isolation, repair and return-to-service steps for water main
breaks found during and after storms.
2.0 SCOPE

Applies to distribution mains 2 in. and larger in all SGW water systems while an event is
declared under GEP 00.010. Routine breaks outside declared events follow the district repair
practice.
3.0 RESPONSIBILITIES
3.1 Water Incident Lead: sets repair priority across districts; orders every valve isolation.

3.2 Water Branch Director or district supervisor: assigns repair crews and reports progress each
    operational period.

3.3 Water Compliance Officer: decides on boil water advisories or notices with the Water
    Incident Lead.
3.4 Repair Crew Foreman: makes the site safe, isolates on order, repairs and flushes.
6.0 PROCEDURE
6.1 Report and triage
6.1.1 Log every reported break with location, size, and time found.
6.1.2 Rank the break by Attachment A.
6.1.3 Report Priority A breaks to the Water Incident Lead at once.
6.2 Make safe
6.2.1 Set traffic control.
6.2.2 Check for downed or tangled conductors. If present, request electric make-safe and wait.
6.2.3 Mark underground utilities. Call 811 with the emergency ticket type.
6.3 Isolation

6.3.1 Identify the valves on the valve map. Count the customers and critical facilities inside
      the shutdown.
6.3.2 Request the isolation from the Water Incident Lead. Give the valve numbers.
6.3.3 Close valves only after the order. Record each valve, turns and time on F-WDS-212.
6.3.4 Notify any hospital or dialysis center inside the shutdown before closing.
6.4 Pressure and water quality
6.4.1 Read pressure at the nearest hydrant before and after isolation.

6.4.2 If pressure at any service connection fell below the state floor, notify the Water
      Compliance Officer within 1 h.

6.4.3 The boil water evaluation then follows WQC 07.114 (Georgia) or WQC 07.120 (South
      Carolina).
6.5 Repair and return to service
6.5.1 Keep the trench dewatered below the pipe.
6.5.2 Swab new fittings and pipe with 1 percent hypochlorite solution.

6.5.3 Repair with a full-circle clamp or a cut-in sleeve. Replace a section where the barrel is
      split more than 12 in.
6.5.4 Open valves slowly on the Water Incident Lead's order.

1.0 PURPOSE

This procedure sets how mains are flushed from the source outward after pressure in a zone fell
below the state floor, before sampling to lift a boil water advisory or notice.
2.0 SCOPE

Applies to all SGW water systems after a low-pressure event, a main break repair, or a zone
isolation. Routine unidirectional flushing programs follow the annual flushing plan.
3.0 RESPONSIBILITIES
3.1 Water Incident Lead: approves the flushing sequence and orders valve operations.
3.2 Flushing Crew Leader: runs the sequence and keeps the flushing record.

3.3 Water Quality Technician: reads residual and turbidity at each hydrant and draws
    bacteriological samples per WQC 07.130.
3.4 Water Compliance Officer: confirms the zone is ready for rescission sampling.

blocks: 2.0 SCOPE

All elevated tanks and standpipes in SGW water systems. Ground storage at treatment plants is
covered by plant procedures.
3.0 RESPONSIBILITIES

3.1 Water Control Room Operator: watches tank levels on SCADA, acknowledges alarms and takes the
    first actions in section 6.

3.2 Distribution Field Operator: verifies level locally and operates altitude and isolation
    valves when directed.
3.3 Water Incident Lead: directs response during declared events and orders any valve isolation.
6.0 PROCEDURE
6.1 High level (H)
6.1.1 Confirm the filling pump station has stopped on its level control.
6.1.2 If pumps are still running, stop the lead pump from SCADA.
6.1.3 Log the event in the control room log.
6.2 High-high level (HH)
6.2.1 Stop all pumps filling the tank.
6.2.2 Dispatch a Distribution Field Operator to check the altitude valve.
6.2.3 If the altitude valve is stuck open, close the tank inlet valve by hand.
6.3 Overflow
6.3.1 Confirm overflow by camera or field report.
6.3.2 Stop filling. Close the inlet valve.
6.3.3 Estimate the volume lost from the level trend and the overflow pipe size.
6.3.4 Notify the Water Compliance Officer. Report any erosion or off-site flow.
6.3.5 Inspect the overflow screen and flap gate before the tank returns to service.
6.4 Low level (L) and low-low level (LL)
6.4.1 Check whether the filling station is in alarm or without power.

6.4.2 If the filling station has lost power, start tank drawdown tracking per WDS 03.240.
      Drawdown is tracked every 15 min.
6.4.3 At LL, inform the Water Incident Lead. Pressure response follows WDS 03.105.
6.4.4 Do not isolate the tank without the Water Incident Lead's order.
6.5 Before a forecast storm

6.5.1 From 48 h before forecast tropical-storm-force winds, raise each tank to between H and HH
      less 0.5 ft.
6.5.2 Check that the overflow screen is in place and the flap gate closes.

6.2.1 Flush the tap 3 min.

6.4.2 If confirmed, call the Water Compliance Officer at once.

6.4.4 The Water Compliance Officer notifies the Georgia EPD district inspector or SCDES Region
      staff the same day. Nights and weekends in Georgia, the Georgia State Emergency Operations
      Center.

6.4.5 The Water Compliance Officer and the Water Incident Lead decide whether a boil water
      advisory (WQC 07.114) or notice (WQC 07.120) is needed.

4.1 Notify the RC before shedding load, or at once if shed is automatic or immediate.
4.2 Notify neighbouring TOPs and the Balancing Authority on the RC call.
4.3 Notify the Duty Manager and the PIO within 15 minutes.
5.0 MITIGATION STEPS
5.1 Outage Recall
Cancel or recall planned transmission and generation outages where this relieves the Emergency.
5.2 Reconfiguration
Reconfigure the transmission system per TSO 06.110 switching rules.
5.3 Redispatch
Request generation redispatch from the Balancing Authority.
5.4 Manual Load Shed

5.4.1 Shed load in rotating blocks from Attachment 2. Each block shall be shed within 10 minutes
      of the order.
5.4.2 Rotate blocks every 30 to 45 minutes to limit customer outage time.

5.4.3 Feeders serving hospitals and water pump stations are excluded from rotating load-shed
      blocks. Attachment 1 lists FDR-AIK-2207 and FDR-AIK-2231.

5.4.4 Feeders with UFLS or UVLS relays are kept out of manual blocks where possible. Overlap is
      listed in Attachment 2, column 5.

CAUTION: Do not place an excluded feeder in a block to meet a MW target. Use the next block
         instead.
5.5 Cold and Extreme Weather

Before a forecast cold snap below 20 F or a hurricane, the Manager, Transmission Operations
reviews block MW values against the forecast load and reissues Attachment 2 if any block changes
by more than 15 percent.
6.0 RECORDS

Operator logs, RC call recordings and block rotation logs are kept for 3 years plus the current
year.

blocks: 4.0 NOTIFICATIONS
4.1 Notify the RC before shedding load, or at once if shed is automatic or immediate.
4.2 Notify neighbouring TOPs and the Balancing Authority on the RC call.
4.3 Notify the Duty Manager and the PIO within 15 minutes.
5.0 MITIGATION STEPS
5.1 Outage Recall
Cancel or recall planned transmission and generation outages where this relieves the Emergency.
5.2 Reconfiguration
Reconfigure the transmission system per TSO 06.110 switching rules.
5.3 Redispatch
Request generation redispatch from the Balancing Authority.
5.4 Manual Load Shed

5.4.1 Shed load in rotating blocks from Attachment 2. Each block shall be shed within 10 minutes
      of the order.
5.4.2 Rotate blocks every 30 to 45 minutes to limit customer outage time.

5.4.3 Feeders serving hospitals and water pump stations are excluded from rotating load-shed
      blocks. Attachment 1 lists FDR-AIK-2207 and FDR-AIK-2231.

5.4.4 Feeders with UFLS or UVLS relays are kept out of manual blocks where possible. Overlap is
      listed in Attachment 2, column 5.

CAUTION: Do not place an excluded feeder in a block to meet a MW target. Use the next block
         instead.
5.5 Cold and Extreme Weather

Before a forecast cold snap below 20 F or a hurricane, the Manager, Transmission Operations
reviews block MW values against the forecast load and reissues Attachment 2 if any block changes
by more than 15 percent.
6.0 RECORDS

Operator logs, RC call recordings and block rotation logs are kept for 3 years plus the current
year.

BOIL WATER NOTICE - [SERIAL] [SYSTEM NAME], PWS ID [PWS ID] Issued [DATE] at [TIME]

Due to [CAUSE], customers in the area listed below may have experienced low water pressure or a
loss of water service beginning [START]. Out of an abundance of caution, SGW, in coordination
with the South Carolina Department of Environmental Services (SCDES), advises affected customers
to boil water used for drinking and cooking until further notice.
Affected area: [AREA]

What should I do? Bring water to a rolling boil and keep it boiling for one minute. Let it cool
before use. Use boiled or bottled water for drinking, making ice, brushing teeth, washing food
and making baby formula. Discard ice, beverages and formula made with tap water during the
affected period. Water is safe for bathing if you do not swallow it. Take care with infants and
young children. Do not use home filters as a substitute for boiling.

When will this end? SGW crews are restoring service. Bacteriological testing will be completed
before the notice is lifted. We expect this to take [EXPECTED DURATION] after pressure is
restored.
For questions call SGW Customer Service at [CONTACT].
We will provide the next update at: [NEXT UPDATE]

The Boil Water Notice issued [ISSUE DATE] for [AREA] is lifted. Water pressure has been
restored, lines have been flushed and bacteriological tests show the water meets drinking water
standards.

Customers should run cold water taps for 2 minutes before use and discard ice made during the
notice.
For questions call SGW Customer Service at [CONTACT].

blocks: 1.0 PURPOSE

This procedure sets how SGW issues and lifts a boil water notice (BWN) for its South Carolina
water systems.
2.0 SCOPE

All SGW public water systems in South Carolina, including the Aiken district. Georgia systems
follow WQC 07.114.
3.0 RESPONSIBILITIES

Water Compliance Officer: decides on the BWN with the Water Incident Lead. Notifies SCDES.
Requests release of the notice.
Water Incident Lead: co-approves the notice. Directs repair, flushing and isolation.
Director, Corporate Communications: distributes the approved notice.
Water Quality Technician: collects bacteriological samples. Completes F-WQC-031.
6.0 PROCEDURE
6.1 Decision
6.1.1 Take the low-pressure report from WDS 03.105 section 6.4.

6.1.2 Issue a BWN when pressure at a service connection falls below the 5.1 minimum, or
      integrity is lost.
6.1.3 Map the affected area by zone and street.
6.2 Regulator Notification
6.2.1 Call the SCDES regional drinking-water office during business hours.
6.2.2 After hours, call the SCDES 24-hour emergency line in Attachment B.
6.2.3 Log the name, time and reference number on F-WQC-031.
6.3 Issue the Notice
6.3.1 Draft the notice from Attachment A (full template: PCN 02.032).
6.3.2 The notice is approved by the Water Incident Lead and the Water Compliance Officer.

6.3.3 A verbal notice may go first to critical customers and the county EMA. Release the written
      notice within 4 h.
6.3.4 Give the notice a serial BWN-SC-yymm-nn.
6.3.5 End every notice with the next update time.
6.4 Lifting the Notice
6.4.1 Restore pressure and integrity. Flush per WDS 03.420.
6.4.2 Collect bacteriological samples at sites chosen from WQC 07.130.
6.4.3 Lift the notice only when all total coliform results are negative and SCDES agrees.
6.4.4 Release the lifting notice by the same channels as the original.

blocks: 1.0 PURPOSE

This procedure sets how SGW issues, announces and rescinds a boil water advisory (BWA) for its
Georgia water systems.
2.0 SCOPE

All SGW community water systems permitted by Georgia EPD, including the Richmond district. South
Carolina systems follow WQC 07.120. It does not cover advisories ordered directly by EPD; follow
the EPD order in that case.
3.0 RESPONSIBILITIES

Water Compliance Officer: owns the BWA decision with the Water Incident Lead. Notifies Georgia
EPD. Signs the rescission request.
Water Incident Lead: co-approves the public notice. Directs repair, flushing and isolation.

Director, Corporate Communications: releases the approved notice through the channels in
Attachment A.
Water Quality Technician: collects samples and fills in F-WQC-031.
6.0 PROCEDURE
6.1 Assessment
6.1.1 On a report from WDS 03.105 section 6.4, confirm the reading, time and location.
6.1.2 Issue a BWA when pressure falls below 20 psi or system integrity is lost.
6.1.3 Out of an abundance of caution, include adjoining streets on the same main.
6.1.4 Define the affected area by zone and street. Use the zone map in WQC 07.130.
6.2 Regulator Notification

6.2.1 Notify the Georgia EPD district inspector by phone before the public notice is released,
      where possible.

6.2.2 Nights and weekends, contact the Georgia State Emergency Operations Center. Ask that the
      EPD on-call be paged.
6.2.3 Record the name, time and number called on F-WQC-031.
6.2.4 Send the written notice copy to the district office within 24 h.
6.3 Public Notice
6.3.1 Prepare the notice from PCN 02.031.

6.3.2 The public notice is approved by the Water Incident Lead and the Water Compliance Officer.
      Both names and times go on F-WQC-031.

6.3.3 Communications releases the notice through the Attachment A channels within 2 h of the
      decision.

6.3.4 Phone critical customers in the area directly: hospitals, dialysis centres, nursing homes,
      schools.
6.3.5 Assign the notice serial BWA-GA-yymm-nn from the compliance log.
6.3.6 State the next update time in every notice.
6.4 Rescission
6.4.1 Rescission requires all of the following:
a. system integrity restored and positive pressure held;
b. the affected mains flushed per WDS 03.420;

blocks: 2.0 SCOPE

All SGW potable-water pressure zones in South Carolina and Georgia. It does not apply to
raw-water mains or to fire-line testing.
3.0 RESPONSIBILITIES
Water SCADA Operator: acknowledges pressure alarms and starts section 6.
Water Distribution Supervisor (on call): sends a crew to verify the reading in the field.
Water Incident Lead: directs station, tank and generator actions during an event.

Water Compliance Officer: decides, with the Water Incident Lead, whether a boil water advisory
or notice is issued.
6.0 PROCEDURE
6.1 Alarm
6.1.1 Acknowledge the alarm within 5 min.
6.1.2 Check station status, tank level and any active main break in the zone.
6.1.3 Trend the zone critical point for the past 2 h.
6.2 Field Verification
6.2.1 Send the on-call crew with a calibrated gauge.
6.2.2 Read at the hydrant nearest the critical point. Record the reading, time and hydrant id.
6.2.3 For zones fed by a booster on generator power, read at the station discharge too.
6.3 Restore Pressure
6.3.1 Start standby pumps if available.

6.3.2 If the station has lost power, follow WDS 03.322 (fixed generator) or WDS 03.318 (PS-17
      portable hookup).
6.3.3 Track tank drawdown per WDS 03.240.
6.3.4 Notify critical customers in the zone using DOM 14.140.
6.4 Below the State Minimum

6.4.1 When pressure at a service connection falls below the state minimum, notify the Water
      Compliance Officer within 1 h.

6.4.2 The Water Compliance Officer starts the boil water evaluation under WQC 07.114 (Georgia)
      or WQC 07.120 (South Carolina).

6.4.3 Record the affected streets and zones on the advisory map. Use the zone ids from
      Attachment A.
6.4.4 Keep reading the critical point every 30 min until pressure is above the minimum for 2 h.

CAUTION: Do not start flushing before the boil water decision is made. Flushing can pull
         pressure lower.
6.4.5 Hand the readings to the Water Compliance Officer for the regulator report.

blocks: 4.0 DEFINITIONS AND ABBREVIATIONS
Service connection: the point where the customer service line meets the SGW main.
Heavy flow: fire flow, main flushing or a main break draining the zone.
Low-pressure event: any verified reading below the state minimum in 5.1 or 5.2.
5.0 PRECAUTIONS AND LIMITS

5.1 South Carolina systems: minimum 25 psi at service connections in normal operation, and 20
    psi under heavy flow (SC R.61-58.7.E(7)).
5.2 Georgia systems: minimum 20 psi at all times (Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. 391-3-5-.10).

5.3 The SCADA low-pressure alarm is set at 40 psi at every zone critical point. Do not lower it
    without Water Incident Lead approval.
5.4 The high-pressure alarm is 110 psi. Above 120 psi, isolate the PRV station.

5.5 A SCADA reading alone is not a verified low-pressure event. Confirm it with a field gauge or
    a second sensor.
7.0 RECORDS

SCADA alarm history (kept 3 years by the historian). Field readings on F-WDS-212. Retain 5
years.
8.0 REFERENCES

SC R.61-58.7.E(7); Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. 391-3-5-.10 WQC 07.114; WQC 07.120; WDS 03.240; WDS
03.318; WDS 03.322; DOM 14.140 WDS 03.115 SCADA Communication Loss: Local Manual Operation

4.0 DEFINITIONS

Uprooted-tree break: a main or service torn out by a falling tree root ball. Integrity loss: any
break that drops pressure below the state floor or admits soil or water into the main.
5.0 PRECAUTIONS AND LIMITS
5.1 Crews shall not drive through water over a roadway (GEP 2F.01).

5.2 Where a tree is tangled in overhead conductors, no excavation starts until electric
    make-safe is confirmed per DOM 14.120.
5.3 Trench work deeper than 5 ft requires a protective system.

5.4 State pressure floors: South Carolina 25 psi at service connections in normal operation and
    20 psi under heavy flow (SC R.61-58.7.E(7)); Georgia 20 psi at all times (Ga. Comp. R. &
    Regs. 391-3-5-.10).

blocks: 4.0 DEFINITIONS

Directional (unidirectional) flushing: closing valves so water moves one way, from a clean
source toward the hydrant, at scouring velocity. Pipe volume: the volume of the main segment
between the open source valve and the flushing hydrant.
5.0 PRECAUTIONS AND LIMITS

5.1 Do not start flushing until pressure in the zone has been at or above the state floor for 1
    h and the source tank or station is stable.
5.2 Hydrant discharge shall not flood a roadway or private property. Use diffusers.
5.3 Dechlorinate per Attachment A where discharge can reach a stream or storm inlet.

5.4 CAUTION: Open and close hydrants and valves slowly, over at least 60 s, to avoid water
    hammer.

5.5 State floors: SC 25 psi at service connections in normal operation and 20 psi under heavy
    flow (SC R.61-58.7.E(7)); GA 20 psi at all times (Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. 391-3-5-.10).
7.0 RECORDS
Flushing record (runs, volumes, readings) and F-WDS-212. Retain 10 years with the advisory file.
8.0 REFERENCES
ATTACHMENT A DECHLORINATION

Zones with an elevated tank and a single booster. Ground storage and clearwells are covered by
plant procedures.
3.0 RESPONSIBILITIES
Water Incident Lead: orders isolation valve operations and tanker requests.
Water SCADA Operator: tracks tank level and forecasts the time to the residual-pressure limit.

Residual-pressure limit: the tank level at which the zone critical point reaches the state floor
in WDS 03.105. Values are in Attachment A.
Time to limit: (current level minus limit level) divided by the drawdown rate.

F-WDS-212 Valve Operation Record; SCADA tank trend. Retain 5 years.

ATTACHMENT A TANK PLANNING DATA
Planning rates are average-day demand. Use 1.4 times the rate on a hot day.

Hospital-zone pump station: a water pump station whose pressure zone supplies a hospital listed

Customers restored per crew-hour: customers expected back on a feeder divided by the crew-hours

Priority 1: hospitals and the water pump stations that supply them. Priority 2: 911 centres,

blocks: 6.0 CREW PRE-POSITIONING
6.1 Decision at H-96

6.1.1 At H-96 the Duty Manager and the Logistics Section Chief decide the mutual-aid request and
      the pre-staging plan. This decision was moved from H-72 in Rev F after Hurricane Debby
      (AAR-DEB-24).
6.1.2 The Duty Manager sizes the request from the Event Type and Attachment 3 of GEP 00.010.

6.1.3 The Logistics Section Chief confirms yard capacity (Attachment 4) and lodging per MAL
      05.030.
6.1.4 Place the mutual-aid request through SEE per MAL 05.012.

blocks: 2.0 SCOPE

All de-energized overhead and substation work on SGW lines and equipment during storm
restoration, by SGW, mutual-aid and contract crews. Mutual-aid crews follow this procedure, not
their home rules, while working on the SGW system (briefed under DOM 12.040).
3.0 RESPONSIBILITIES
3.1 The clearance holder (TSO 06.110) decides grounding locations and keeps the ground log.
3.2 Crew members apply and remove grounds as directed by the clearance holder.
3.3 The Staging Area Manager issues inspected ground sets from the yard.
6.0 PROCEDURE
6.1 Before Grounding

6.1.1 Confirm the clearance and every open point by three-part communication with the switching
      desk.
6.1.2 Hold a tailboard. Name the grounding locations and the worker who applies each set.
6.2 Apply

6.2.1 Ground at the work location to build an EPZ: bracket the work, or ground at the pole being
      worked with a cluster bar.

6.2.2 Ground both sides of the work when backfeed is possible, including any section with
      services that could carry customer generator power.
6.2.3 Connect the ground end to the system neutral, cluster bar or station ground grid.
6.2.4 Connect phases nearest to farthest.
6.2.5 Record each ground on the ground log: location, set number, time applied.
6.3 Remove
6.3.1 Confirm all workers are clear.
6.3.2 Remove phase ends farthest to nearest, then the ground end.

6.3.3 Record the removal time. The clearance holder counts sets back before releasing the
      clearance.
6.3.4 Return sets to the yard. Damaged sets are tagged out of service.
6.4 Special Cases

6.4.1 Pad-mounted transformers and underground cable: ground at the elbow with a feed-through
      bushing and a grounding elbow rated per Attachment A.
6.4.2 Substations: connect to the station ground grid at the tagged grounding points only.

6.4.3 Long spans in parallel with an energized line: expect induced voltage. Ground at each end
      of the section and at the work location.

6.4.4 Wire on the ground: ground the conductor on both sides of the break before cutting (DOM
      14.120).

6.1 Before All-Clear
6.1.1 Run the pre-landfall model at each NHC advisory once the Event Type is 1 or 2.
6.1.2 Share the run with the Duty Manager for staffing decisions. Do not publish it.
6.2 Global ETR
6.2.1 Publish the global ETR within 24 h after the all-clear.

6.2.2 State the global ETR as a range: P25, P50 and P75 (range of the 25th, 50th and 75th
      percentiles).
6.2.3 The ETR Specialist proposes the global ETR on F-DOM-121 with the model inputs attached.

6.2.4 The Incident Commander and the Duty Manager approve the global ETR before release. Both
      signatures go on F-DOM-121.

6.2.5 Send the approved range to the Public Information Officer. Release wording follows PCN
      02.044.

6.1 Decide

6.2.1 Logistics orders the heavy haul tractor, escorts and state oversize permits (SCDOT or
      GDOT).

6.3.3 Install relay settings from the Protection Engineer and test trip.

6.3.6 Pick up feeders one at a time per DOM 14.130.
6.4 Site Checks before Energizing
6.4.1 Confirm the trailer is level within 1 degree and the jacks are on cribbing.
6.4.2 Check oil level, nitrogen pressure and cooling fan operation.
6.4.3 Megger the high-side and low-side leads after connection.

      on site until they are.

blocks: 1.0 PURPOSE

This procedure sets how Logistics dispatches portable generators and delivers diesel to SGW
standby and portable generators during declared events.
2.0 SCOPE

Applies to water pump stations, lift stations, tanks with powered controls, and electric
facilities that run on generator power. Does not apply to customer-owned generators, including
hospital standby units such as GEN-HSP-TALLOWBRANCH.
3.0 RESPONSIBILITIES
Logistics Section Chief: owns the fuel plan, vendor call-outs and the generator dispatch log.

Fuel Coordinator (Logistics): receives F-MAL-022 requests, chooses the fuel source, tracks each
delivery to completion.

Water Incident Lead: sets generator priority among water facilities and requests portable
generators. Depot Supervisor, DEP-AIK-GRANITEVILLE: loads FTK-WREN-3 and readies
MGEN-HALBERD-500 for transport.
6.0 PROCEDURE
6.1 Requests
6.1.1 Generator dispatch and fuel requests are made on form F-MAL-022 and logged by Logistics.

6.1.2 The requester gives facility id, generator id, gauge reading, time of reading and load
      (kW).
6.1.3 Fuel Coordinator computes remaining run time from Attachment A.
6.2 Generator dispatch
6.2.1 Water Incident Lead confirms the target site and the connection point per WDS 03.318.
6.2.2 Depot Supervisor starts load-out and reports departure time to Logistics.
6.2.3 Logistics logs dispatched, on-site and running times against the F-MAL-022 number.
6.2.4 NOTE: Hookup and start-up times are set by WDS 03.318 section 6.4, not by this procedure.
6.3 Fuel source selection
6.3.1 Compare the vendor delivery time with the generator's remaining run time.

6.3.2 Where the vendor delivery time is longer than a generator's remaining run time, the SGW
      fuel truck is used first.

6.3.3 Call Altamaha for the next delivery to the same site at the same time, so the truck can be
      released.

6.3.4 Where two sites compete for FTK-WREN-3, the Water Incident Lead sets the order. Sites
      serving a hospital or critical facility per DOM 14.140 go first.
6.3.5 CAUTION: Do not fuel a running generator unless the unit is rated for hot refuelling.
6.4 Records of delivery
6.4.1 Driver records gallons delivered, gauge before and after, and time (24-hour EDT).
6.4.2 Vendor delivery tickets are scanned to the F-MAL-022 record within 12 h.

blocks: 6.0 PROCEDURE
6.1 Start of Run

6.1.1 When a unit starts on loss of grid supply, record the start time and fuel level on
      F-WDS-207.
6.1.2 Report the start to the Water Incident Lead.
6.1.3 Calculate run time remaining using the Attachment A burn rate.
6.2 Monitoring
6.2.1 Read and log the fuel level every 4 h on F-WDS-207 while the generator runs.

6.2.2 Read the sight gauge, not only the SCADA signal. Record both if they differ by more than 5
      percent.
6.2.3 Log load (kW), oil pressure and coolant temperature with each fuel reading.

NOTE: At unmanned stations a roving operator may cover up to three stations. Keep the 4 h
      interval.
6.3 Refuel Request
6.3.1 When the fuel tank falls to 60 percent, raise a refuel request.

6.3.2 Submit the request on F-MAL-022 to the Logistics desk. State unit id, level, burn rate and
      route.

6.3.3 Flag any route that crosses a low-water crossing in GEP 2F.01 Attachment 2. Copperleaf
      Road (PS-38) and Deerwater Spur (PS-52) are on that list.

6.3.4 If run time remaining is shorter than the vendor delivery time, tell Logistics. Logistics
      then sends the SGW fuel truck first (MAL 05.040).
6.3.5 Log the delivery time and gallons received.
6.4 Shutdown
6.4.1 After return to grid supply, run unloaded for 5 min, then stop.
6.4.2 Top off to 95 percent within 24 h.
7.0 RECORDS
F-WDS-207 Generator Run Log; F-MAL-022 fuel request. Retain 5 years.

blocks: 5.0 PROCEDURE
5.1 Call the Water Control Room. Give station, generator id and planned start time.
5.2 Walk down the unit: oil, coolant, belts, battery terminals, fuel leaks, louvers clear.
5.3 Read the fuel gauge. Record it.
5.4 Simulate utility loss at the ATS test switch.
5.5 Confirm transfer within 15 s. Record the time to transfer.

5.6 Run under load for 30 min. Record kW, volts, amps, frequency, oil pressure and coolant
    temperature at 0, 15 and 30 min.
5.7 End the test. Confirm retransfer and the 5 min cooldown.
5.8 Read the fuel gauge again.

5.9 From June 1 to November 30 keep the sub-base tank at or above 90 percent after the test.
    Request fuel on F-MAL-022 if lower.
5.10 Return the unit to AUTO. Call the Water Control Room.

6.3.1 Position the generator on the north pad. Chock the wheels.
6.3.2 Bond the frame to the ground bar.
6.3.3 Verify the MTS is in the OFF (centre) position.
6.3.4 Open utility breaker CB-1 and apply the station lock.

6.3.6 Start the generator. Allow 5 min warm-up at no load.
6.3.7 Move the MTS to GENERATOR.

6.3.9 Confirm discharge pressure of 68 to 74 psi.

      time is 150 min (Attachment A); report any overrun and its cause to Logistics.
6.4.2 Log fuel, load and discharge pressure every 4 h on F-WDS-207.
6.4.3 Request fuel at the threshold in WDS 03.322 section 6.3.
6.5 Return to Grid Supply

6.5.1 Return only on the Water Incident Lead's order, after Distribution Operations confirms
      FDR-AIK-2207 is stable.
6.5.2 Stop pump 2, then pump 1.
6.5.3 Move the MTS to OFF, then to UTILITY. Close CB-1.
6.5.4 Restart the pumps on grid power. Run the generator unloaded for 5 min, then stop it.
6.5.5 Leave the generator connected for 12 h if more weather is forecast.

    follows MAL 05.040 section 6.

5.5 Where neither pre-delivery nor an alternate route is possible, Logistics shall notify the
    Water Incident Lead, who decides on portable-generator relocation or controlled shutdown.

5.6 Staging sites shall sit outside the FEMA 100-year floodplain. STG-AIK-SANDHILL-YARD and

blocks: 4.0 DEFINITIONS AND ABBREVIATIONS

MTS: manual transfer switch. PS-17 has a manual transfer switch and no automatic transfer switch
(ATS).
Hookup lead time: time from dispatch of the portable generator to pumping on generator power.

Residual-pressure limit: tank level below which zone pressure cannot be held (WDS 03.240
Attachment A).
5.0 PRECAUTIONS AND LIMITS

5.1 Plan on a hookup lead time of 150 min from dispatch to pumping. This covers travel, cable
    connection and manual transfer.

5.2 The station draws 412 kW at two-pump duty. MGEN-HALBERD-500 (500 kW) runs both pumps; do not
    start pump 3 on generator power.

5.3 CAUTION: The MTS is break-before-make. Open the utility-side breaker before closing the
    generator side. Backfeed onto FDR-AIK-2207 endangers line crews.
5.4 Ground the generator frame to the station ground bar before cables are landed.

5.5 Do not run the generator in the dry well. Park it on the north pad, at least 15 ft from the
    louvres.
6.0 PROCEDURE
6.3.1 Position the generator on the north pad. Chock the wheels.
6.3.2 Bond the frame to the ground bar.
6.3.3 Verify the MTS is in the OFF (centre) position.
6.3.4 Open utility breaker CB-1 and apply the station lock.

6.3.5 Land the cables at the generator connection cabinet. Check phase rotation with the
      rotation meter.
6.3.6 Start the generator. Allow 5 min warm-up at no load.
6.3.7 Move the MTS to GENERATOR.
6.3.8 Start pump 1, then pump 2 after 60 s.
6.3.9 Confirm discharge pressure of 68 to 74 psi.
6.3.10 Report "PS-17 pumping on generator" and the time to the Water Incident Lead.
6.4 Running on Generator Power

6.4.1 Record the pumping start time against the dispatch time. The planned hookup and start-up
      time is 150 min (Attachment A); report any overrun and its cause to Logistics.
6.4.2 Log fuel, load and discharge pressure every 4 h on F-WDS-207.
6.4.3 Request fuel at the threshold in WDS 03.322 section 6.3.
6.5 Return to Grid Supply

6.5.1 Return only on the Water Incident Lead's order, after Distribution Operations confirms
      FDR-AIK-2207 is stable.
6.5.2 Stop pump 2, then pump 1.
6.5.3 Move the MTS to OFF, then to UTILITY. Close CB-1.
6.5.4 Restart the pumps on grid power. Run the generator unloaded for 5 min, then stop it.
6.5.5 Leave the generator connected for 12 h if more weather is forecast.

blocks: 2.0 SCOPE

It applies to diesel standby generators at SGW booster and pump stations in South Carolina and
Georgia. Covered units include GEN-PS38-COPPERLEAF and GEN-PS52-DEERWATER; the full list is in
Attachment A.

It does not apply to portable generators. For PS-17 see WDS 03.318; for monthly load tests see
WDS 03.350.
3.0 RESPONSIBILITIES
Water Incident Lead: approves refuel priority when several stations need fuel at once.
Station Operator: reads and logs fuel level, raises refuel requests.
Water SCADA Operator: watches remote tank-level signals and alerts the Station Operator.
Logistics Section Chief: assigns the vendor or the SGW fuel truck per MAL 05.040.
6.0 PROCEDURE
6.1 Start of Run

6.1.1 When a unit starts on loss of grid supply, record the start time and fuel level on
      F-WDS-207.
6.1.2 Report the start to the Water Incident Lead.
6.1.3 Calculate run time remaining using the Attachment A burn rate.
6.2 Monitoring
6.2.1 Read and log the fuel level every 4 h on F-WDS-207 while the generator runs.

6.2.2 Read the sight gauge, not only the SCADA signal. Record both if they differ by more than 5
      percent.
6.2.3 Log load (kW), oil pressure and coolant temperature with each fuel reading.

NOTE: At unmanned stations a roving operator may cover up to three stations. Keep the 4 h
      interval.
6.3 Refuel Request
6.3.1 When the fuel tank falls to 60 percent, raise a refuel request.

6.3.2 Submit the request on F-MAL-022 to the Logistics desk. State unit id, level, burn rate and
      route.

6.3.3 Flag any route that crosses a low-water crossing in GEP 2F.01 Attachment 2. Copperleaf
      Road (PS-38) and Deerwater Spur (PS-52) are on that list.

6.3.4 If run time remaining is shorter than the vendor delivery time, tell Logistics. Logistics
      then sends the SGW fuel truck first (MAL 05.040).
6.3.5 Log the delivery time and gallons received.
6.4 Shutdown
6.4.1 After return to grid supply, run unloaded for 5 min, then stop.
6.4.2 Top off to 95 percent within 24 h.

blocks: 4.0 DEFINITIONS

Flow-paced feed: metering pump speed set by a 4-20 mA signal from the station flow meter. Day
tank: the small tank feeding the metering pump directly.
5.0 PRECAUTIONS AND LIMITS

5.1 Hypochlorite metering pumps shall be on the generator-backed panel. Confirm this at each
    monthly test under WDS 03.350.

5.2 A metering pump that restarts before flow is established can overfeed. Never start feed with
    zero station flow.

5.3 Target free chlorine residual leaving the station is 1.2 to 2.0 mg/L. The distribution
    minimum is 0.2 mg/L in Georgia (Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. 391-3-5-.14); see WQC 07.140 for both
    states.

5.4 CAUTION: Hypochlorite off-gasses when heated. Keep the chemical room vent fan on the
    generator panel running.
5.5 Store no more than 30 days of hypochlorite at a station. It loses strength in summer heat.
6.0 PROCEDURE
6.1 On transfer to generator
6.1.1 Confirm pumps restarted and flow is above 150 gpm.
6.1.2 Confirm the metering pump is running and its stroke counter is moving.
6.1.3 Check the calibration column. Record the draw-down rate in gal/h.
6.1.4 Take a free chlorine reading at the station discharge tap within 30 min.
6.2 Flow-paced restart sequence
6.2.1 If feed did not restart, wait until station flow is stable for 2 min.
6.2.2 Start the metering pump in HAND at 25 percent speed.
6.2.3 After 5 min, switch to AUTO (flow-paced).
6.2.4 Recheck residual after 30 min.
6.3 While on generator power
6.3.1 Read the day tank level every 4 h with the generator readings.

6.3.2 Refill the day tank at 25 percent. Do not let it run dry; air in the suction line stops
      feed.
6.3.3 Take a residual at the discharge every 8 h and at the far zone point once per day.

6.3.4 If the discharge residual is below 1.0 mg/L, raise the feed rate by 10 percent and recheck
      in 30 min.

6.3.5 If any distribution reading is below the state minimum, notify the Water Compliance
      Officer.
6.4 On return to grid supply
6.4.1 Confirm feed restarted after retransfer.
6.4.2 Take a discharge residual within 30 min.
6.4.3 Log the end of generator operation in the feed log.

1.0 PURPOSE

This procedure sets how SGW patrols the electric system after a storm and records damage. Patrol
results feed crew assignment and the ETR model (DOM 14.206).
6.0 PROCEDURE
6.1 Start of Patrol
6.1.1 The Duty Manager orders patrol start after the all-clear.
6.1.2 The Damage Assessment Coordinator issues patrol areas on the ICS 204.
6.2 Patrol Order
Patrol in this order:
a. Transmission lines.
b. Substations.
c. Feeder trunks serving critical facilities (DOM 14.140 registry; DOM 14.215 Attachment A).
d. Laterals.
The order may change only on Duty Manager instruction, recorded on the ICS 214.
6.3 Recording
6.3.1 Record each damaged asset on F-DOM-118 with the asset id, location and damage state.
6.3.2 Record the damage state as slight, moderate, extensive or complete.
6.3.3 Take at least two photos per asset: one wide, one close.
6.3.4 Upload records at least every 2 h, or when signal allows.
6.4 Progress Reporting
6.4.1 Report percent of circuits patrolled by region at each operational period.

6.4.2 Notify the ETR Specialist when a region reaches 80 percent of circuits patrolled (DOM
      14.206 section 6.3).
6.5 Photo Review

6.5.1 Damage-assessment photos are queued for review in order of the image-model damage score,
      highest first.

6.5.2 A person confirms every damage state. The model score orders the queue only; it never sets
      a damage state.

6.5.3 Where the reviewer disagrees with the assessor, the reviewer's state stands and the change
      is noted on F-DOM-118.
6.5.4 Hold the queue at 400 photos or more per reviewer and call in relief reviewers.

1.0 PURPOSE

Sets how SGW decides on, moves and connects a mobile substation when a distribution substation
transformer or bus is lost.
2.0 SCOPE

Mobile substations owned by SGW and those received through mutual assistance. Applies to 115-23
kV and 115-12 kV distribution substations.
6.0 PROCEDURE
6.1 Decide

6.1.1 The Duty Manager requests a mobile when the fixed transformer will be out longer than 48 h
      and feeders cannot be carried on adjacent substations.

6.1.2 The Manager, Transmission Operations assigns the unit and records the decision in the
      incident log.

6.1.3 Restoration priority (DOM 14.215) guides which substation gets the unit when two request
      it.
6.2 Move

6.2.1 Logistics orders the heavy haul tractor, escorts and state oversize permits (SCDOT or
      GDOT).
6.2.2 For moves over 40 mi, survey the route for bridge limits, overhead clearance and flooding.
6.2.3 Check road closures on F-MAL-030 entries and county EOC reports.
6.3 Connect
6.3.1 Place the trailer per the site layout drawing in the substation file.
6.3.2 Bond the trailer to the station ground grid at two points.
6.3.3 Install relay settings from the Protection Engineer and test trip.
6.3.4 Connect high-side and low-side under a clearance per TSO 06.110. Ground per TSO 06.130.
6.3.5 Energize from the high side with low-side breakers open.
6.3.6 Pick up feeders one at a time per DOM 14.130.
6.4 Site Checks before Energizing
6.4.1 Confirm the trailer is level within 1 degree and the jacks are on cribbing.
6.4.2 Check oil level, nitrogen pressure and cooling fan operation.
6.4.3 Megger the high-side and low-side leads after connection.

6.4.4 Confirm SCADA points for the mobile breakers are reporting, or post a substation operator
      on site until they are.

blocks: 1.0 LETTER OF PROMULGATION
To all SGW employees, contractors and mutual-assistance partners working under SGW direction:

The SGW Emergency Response Plan (ERP) is hereby promulgated as the governing plan for
emergencies that affect SGW electric and water service in South Carolina and east Georgia.

The ERP consists of the base plan chapters (GEP 00 to GEP 09), the hazard annexes (GEP 2F, 2H,
2T, 2W and 2X) and the owner-manual procedures they call. It applies to every district, from
Aiken and Richmond to the coastal service area.

The ERP adopts the Incident Command System (ICS). Positions named in the plan are ICS positions
and act with the authority the plan gives them, regardless of normal reporting lines.

The ERP supersedes all prior editions and any district storm plan that conflicts with it.
District supplements remain valid where they add local detail and do not change a threshold,
role or time limit.

Each manual owner shall review the documents in their manual before 30 April of each year. The
review is complete when the owner has signed the review entry in DocCtl, whether or not a change
results.

Every person assigned an ERP position shall read the base plan and the annexes for their
function before
1 June of each year, and confirm that reading in the Learning Management System.
This promulgation remains in effect until reissued.
Signed: Vice President, Emergency Management (Wingard, Lorraine T.), 2024-05-06.
3.0 REVISION AND CHANGE CONTROL

3.1 A revision advances the letter, carries a new effective date and requires new approvals.
    Letters I, O, Q and S are not used.

3.2 A change (Chg) replaces limited pages only. It keeps the revision letter and the original
    effective date and needs no new signatures. Cite it as revision and change, as in GEP 2H.01
    Rev E/1.

3.3 A change shall not alter a threshold, a time limit, an approver or an Event Type criterion.
    Those need a revision.

3.4 The superseded revision stays in DocCtl marked SUPERSEDED and is retained for record for 10
    years.

3.5 Interim instructions during an event are issued as Operations Bulletins (OB-yy-nn) with an
    expiry date. A bulletin overrides the named procedure section only until it expires.

3.6 After-action corrective actions that change the ERP are tracked to the revision that closes
    them (see GEP 07.010 section 6).

blocks: 4.0 DEFINITIONS

Uprooted-tree break: a main or service torn out by a falling tree root ball. Integrity loss: any
break that drops pressure below the state floor or admits soil or water into the main.
5.0 PRECAUTIONS AND LIMITS
5.1 Crews shall not drive through water over a roadway (GEP 2F.01).

5.2 Where a tree is tangled in overhead conductors, no excavation starts until electric
    make-safe is confirmed per DOM 14.120.
5.3 Trench work deeper than 5 ft requires a protective system.

5.4 State pressure floors: South Carolina 25 psi at service connections in normal operation and
    20 psi under heavy flow (SC R.61-58.7.E(7)); Georgia 20 psi at all times (Ga. Comp. R. &
    Regs. 391-3-5-.10).
6.0 PROCEDURE
6.1 Report and triage
6.1.1 Log every reported break with location, size, and time found.
6.1.2 Rank the break by Attachment A.
6.1.3 Report Priority A breaks to the Water Incident Lead at once.
6.2 Make safe
6.2.1 Set traffic control.
6.2.2 Check for downed or tangled conductors. If present, request electric make-safe and wait.
6.2.3 Mark underground utilities. Call 811 with the emergency ticket type.
6.3 Isolation

6.3.1 Identify the valves on the valve map. Count the customers and critical facilities inside
      the shutdown.
6.3.2 Request the isolation from the Water Incident Lead. Give the valve numbers.
6.3.3 Close valves only after the order. Record each valve, turns and time on F-WDS-212.
6.3.4 Notify any hospital or dialysis center inside the shutdown before closing.
6.4 Pressure and water quality
6.4.1 Read pressure at the nearest hydrant before and after isolation.

6.4.2 If pressure at any service connection fell below the state floor, notify the Water
      Compliance Officer within 1 h.

6.4.3 The boil water evaluation then follows WQC 07.114 (Georgia) or WQC 07.120 (South
      Carolina).
6.5 Repair and return to service
6.5.1 Keep the trench dewatered below the pipe.
6.5.2 Swab new fittings and pipe with 1 percent hypochlorite solution.

6.5.3 Repair with a full-circle clamp or a cut-in sleeve. Replace a section where the barrel is
      split more than 12 in.
6.5.4 Open valves slowly on the Water Incident Lead's order.

This procedure connects a portable generator to PS-17 Pellicott Road Booster when grid supply is
lost.
2.0 SCOPE

PS-17 has no onsite generator. On loss of grid supply, a portable generator is connected under
this procedure.

PS-17 serves pressure zone WZ-PS17-CEDARFALL and fills tank TNK-PS17-CEDARFALL. The zone
includes Tallow Branch hospital (HSP-AIK-TALLOWBRANCH). PS-17 is supplied by feeder
FDR-AIK-2207.

This procedure does not apply to stations with a fixed standby generator; see WDS 03.322 for
those units.
6.0 PROCEDURE
6.1 Loss of Grid Supply

6.1.1 On a PS-17 power-fail alarm, the Water SCADA Operator confirms the fault with the
      Distribution Operations storm desk. Record the FDR-AIK-2207 status and the expected
      restoration, if known.

6.1.2 The Water SCADA Operator reports TNK-PS17-CEDARFALL level and WZ-PS17-CEDARFALL pressure
      to the Water Incident Lead every 15 min. Track drawdown per WDS 03.240.

6.1.3 If feeder restoration is not confirmed within 30 min, the Water Incident Lead orders the
      dispatch of the portable generator. Do not wait for low pressure.

6.1.4 When zone pressure falls below 35 psi, notify the Tallow Branch hospital facilities
      manager. Use the after-hours line in Attachment B. Log the time and name on F-WDS-207.

NOTE: The hospital runs its own standby generator (GEN-HSP-TALLOWBRANCH) for power. Its water
      supply still depends on PS-17.

6.1.5 If the tank will reach its residual-pressure limit before pumping can resume, request a
      potable-water tanker for the hospital per WDS 03.240 section 6.3.

6.2.1 The Water Incident Lead raises the dispatch request on F-MAL-022 and calls the Logistics
      Section Chief.

6.2.2 Logistics releases MGEN-HALBERD-500 from DEP-AIK-GRANITEVILLE with a full belly tank and

blocks: 4.0 DEFINITIONS

Equipotential zone (EPZ): grounding arranged so that a worker is never in series with a path for
fault current.
Ground set: clamps, ferrules and cable rated for the available fault current.

Backfeed: voltage returning from the secondary side, often from customer-owned portable
generators.
5.0 PRECAUTIONS AND LIMITS
5.1 Ground only after a clearance has been issued and a Hot Line Hold or open point is in place.
5.2 Test for absence of voltage with a tested detector immediately before applying grounds.
5.3 Use ground sets rated for the location per Attachment A.

5.4 Do not use a ground set that has a broken strand at the ferrule, a cracked clamp or missing
    inspection tag.
5.5 Attach the ground end first; remove it last. Use a hot stick for all phase connections.

CAUTION: storm damage creates crossed circuits and customer generator backfeed. Treat every
         conductor as energized until grounded.
6.0 PROCEDURE
6.1 Before Grounding

6.1.1 Confirm the clearance and every open point by three-part communication with the switching
      desk.
6.1.2 Hold a tailboard. Name the grounding locations and the worker who applies each set.
6.2 Apply

6.2.1 Ground at the work location to build an EPZ: bracket the work, or ground at the pole being
      worked with a cluster bar.

6.2.2 Ground both sides of the work when backfeed is possible, including any section with
      services that could carry customer generator power.
6.2.3 Connect the ground end to the system neutral, cluster bar or station ground grid.
6.2.4 Connect phases nearest to farthest.
6.2.5 Record each ground on the ground log: location, set number, time applied.
6.3 Remove
6.3.1 Confirm all workers are clear.
6.3.2 Remove phase ends farthest to nearest, then the ground end.

6.3.3 Record the removal time. The clearance holder counts sets back before releasing the
      clearance.
6.3.4 Return sets to the yard. Damaged sets are tagged out of service.
6.4 Special Cases

6.4.1 Pad-mounted transformers and underground cable: ground at the elbow with a feed-through
      bushing and a grounding elbow rated per Attachment A.
6.4.2 Substations: connect to the station ground grid at the tagged grounding points only.

6.4.3 Long spans in parallel with an energized line: expect induced voltage. Ground at each end
      of the section and at the work location.

6.4.4 Wire on the ground: ground the conductor on both sides of the break before cutting (DOM
      14.120).

blocks: REVISION SUMMARY
1.0 PURPOSE

This procedure sets how SGW develops, approves, releases and revises estimated times of
restoration (ETRs) after a storm.
6.0 PROCEDURE
6.1 Before All-Clear
6.1.1 Run the pre-landfall model at each NHC advisory once the Event Type is 1 or 2.
6.1.2 Share the run with the Duty Manager for staffing decisions. Do not publish it.
6.2 Global ETR
6.2.1 Publish the global ETR within 24 h after the all-clear.

6.2.2 State the global ETR as a range: P25, P50 and P75 (range of the 25th, 50th and 75th
      percentiles).
6.2.3 The ETR Specialist proposes the global ETR on F-DOM-121 with the model inputs attached.

6.2.4 The Incident Commander and the Duty Manager approve the global ETR before release. Both
      signatures go on F-DOM-121.

6.2.5 Send the approved range to the Public Information Officer. Release wording follows PCN
      02.044.
NOTE: The P50 is the headline time in media statements. P25 and P75 are given as the range.
6.3 Regional ETRs

6.3.1 Regional ETRs follow once damage assessment has patrolled 80 percent of circuits in the
      region.

6.3.2 Use the patrol completion count from the Damage Assessment Coordinator, not crew
      estimates.
6.3.3 Approve and release regional ETRs as in 6.2.3 to 6.2.5.
6.4 Revision
6.4.1 Re-run the model at each operational period change.
6.4.2 Revise a published ETR when the P50 moves by more than 12 h.

blocks: 1.0 LETTER OF PROMULGATION
To all SGW employees, contractors and mutual-assistance partners working under SGW direction:

The SGW Emergency Response Plan (ERP) is hereby promulgated as the governing plan for
emergencies that affect SGW electric and water service in South Carolina and east Georgia.

The ERP consists of the base plan chapters (GEP 00 to GEP 09), the hazard annexes (GEP 2F, 2H,
2T, 2W and 2X) and the owner-manual procedures they call. It applies to every district, from
Aiken and Richmond to the coastal service area.

The ERP adopts the Incident Command System (ICS). Positions named in the plan are ICS positions
and act with the authority the plan gives them, regardless of normal reporting lines.

The ERP supersedes all prior editions and any district storm plan that conflicts with it.
District supplements remain valid where they add local detail and do not change a threshold,
role or time limit.

Each manual owner shall review the documents in their manual before 30 April of each year. The
review is complete when the owner has signed the review entry in DocCtl, whether or not a change
results.

Every person assigned an ERP position shall read the base plan and the annexes for their
function before
1 June of each year, and confirm that reading in the Learning Management System.
This promulgation remains in effect until reissued.
Signed: Vice President, Emergency Management (Wingard, Lorraine T.), 2024-05-06.
3.0 REVISION AND CHANGE CONTROL

3.1 A revision advances the letter, carries a new effective date and requires new approvals.
    Letters I, O, Q and S are not used.

3.2 A change (Chg) replaces limited pages only. It keeps the revision letter and the original
    effective date and needs no new signatures. Cite it as revision and change, as in GEP 2H.01
    Rev E/1.

3.3 A change shall not alter a threshold, a time limit, an approver or an Event Type criterion.
    Those need a revision.

3.4 The superseded revision stays in DocCtl marked SUPERSEDED and is retained for record for 10
    years.

3.5 Interim instructions during an event are issued as Operations Bulletins (OB-yy-nn) with an
    expiry date. A bulletin overrides the named procedure section only until it expires.

3.6 After-action corrective actions that change the ERP are tracked to the revision that closes
    them (see GEP 07.010 section 6).

6.0 PROCEDURE
6.1 Before the event

6.1.1 At least 72 h before forecast impact, count storm kits and critical items against the
      storm minimums.
6.1.2 Order the shortfall from the alliance suppliers.
6.1.3 Move storm kits to the staging yard laydowns per MAL 05.020.

6.3.1 Report the shortfall item, quantity and district to Logistics.

      14.215).
6.3.3 Transfers between storerooms go on the next scheduled runner.
6.4 Returns and close-out
6.4.1 Crews return unused material before release (MAL 05.060).
6.4.2 Inspect returned material. Scrap damaged items.
6.4.3 Reconcile issues against completed work within 30 days after the event.
6.5 Water material
6.5.1 Repair clamps, couplings and valve parts for water mains are issued on the same issue log.
6.5.2 Water Branch requests material through Logistics, not directly from electric storerooms.

6.6.1 Storerooms stay open 24 h while emergency issue mode is in effect.

blocks: 4.0 DEFINITIONS

Interruption: loss of electric service to one or more customers, measured from the first OMS
outage record to final restoration of the last customer in the event.
After-action timeline: the time-stamped event sequence assembled for the AAR, per GEP 07.010.
5.0 PRECAUTIONS AND LIMITS
5.1 Under SC 103-314, a full report is filed when an interruption lasts longer than 6 h.
5.2 Customer counts in any notice shall match the OMS count at the stated as-of time.
5.3 Restoration figures shall match the latest released global ETR range per PCN 02.044.
5.4 Do not include estimates that the Incident Commander has not approved.
6.0 PROCEDURE
6.1 Initial notice
6.1.1 The initial notice is sent by the Compliance function.

6.1.2 Duty Manager gives the Compliance function the outage start time, area, customers out and
      suspected cause.

6.1.3 Compliance function sends the notice by e-mail and phone to the ORS and SC PSC duty
      contacts.
6.1.4 Log the time sent and the person reached on the reporting log.
6.1.5 NOTE: During Event Types 1 and 2, send an update with each global ETR release.
6.2 Track duration
6.2.1 Compliance function monitors the event in OMS.
6.2.2 When the interruption passes 6 h, open a full-report file.
6.2.3 Set the report due date in the compliance calendar.
6.3 Full report
6.3.1 The full report is drafted from the after-action timeline.
6.3.2 Planning Section supplies the timeline within 10 business days of event close.
6.3.3 Draft content per Attachment A.
6.3.4 Duty Manager and Planning Section check figures.
6.3.5 Incident Commander reviews; Compliance function files.
6.3.6 Keep the filed copy and transmittal with the incident file.

The SGW Emergency Response Plan (ERP) is hereby promulgated as the governing plan for
emergencies that affect SGW electric and water service in South Carolina and east Georgia.

The ERP consists of the base plan chapters (GEP 00 to GEP 09), the hazard annexes (GEP 2F, 2H,
2T, 2W and 2X) and the owner-manual procedures they call. It applies to every district, from
Aiken and Richmond to the coastal service area.

The ERP adopts the Incident Command System (ICS). Positions named in the plan are ICS positions
and act with the authority the plan gives them, regardless of normal reporting lines.

The ERP supersedes all prior editions and any district storm plan that conflicts with it.
District supplements remain valid where they add local detail and do not change a threshold,
role or time limit.

Each manual owner shall review the documents in their manual before 30 April of each year. The
review is complete when the owner has signed the review entry in DocCtl, whether or not a change
results.

Every person assigned an ERP position shall read the base plan and the annexes for their
function before
1 June of each year, and confirm that reading in the Learning Management System.
This promulgation remains in effect until reissued.
Signed: Vice President, Emergency Management (Wingard, Lorraine T.), 2024-05-06.

blocks: 1.0 PURPOSE

This procedure sets how Logistics dispatches portable generators and delivers diesel to SGW
standby and portable generators during declared events.
2.0 SCOPE

Applies to water pump stations, lift stations, tanks with powered controls, and electric
facilities that run on generator power. Does not apply to customer-owned generators, including
hospital standby units such as GEN-HSP-TALLOWBRANCH.
3.0 RESPONSIBILITIES
Logistics Section Chief: owns the fuel plan, vendor call-outs and the generator dispatch log.

Fuel Coordinator (Logistics): receives F-MAL-022 requests, chooses the fuel source, tracks each
delivery to completion.

Water Incident Lead: sets generator priority among water facilities and requests portable
generators. Depot Supervisor, DEP-AIK-GRANITEVILLE: loads FTK-WREN-3 and readies
MGEN-HALBERD-500 for transport.
6.0 PROCEDURE
6.1 Requests
6.1.1 Generator dispatch and fuel requests are made on form F-MAL-022 and logged by Logistics.

6.1.2 The requester gives facility id, generator id, gauge reading, time of reading and load
      (kW).
6.1.3 Fuel Coordinator computes remaining run time from Attachment A.
6.2 Generator dispatch
6.2.1 Water Incident Lead confirms the target site and the connection point per WDS 03.318.
6.2.2 Depot Supervisor starts load-out and reports departure time to Logistics.
6.2.3 Logistics logs dispatched, on-site and running times against the F-MAL-022 number.
6.2.4 NOTE: Hookup and start-up times are set by WDS 03.318 section 6.4, not by this procedure.
6.3 Fuel source selection
6.3.1 Compare the vendor delivery time with the generator's remaining run time.

6.3.2 Where the vendor delivery time is longer than a generator's remaining run time, the SGW
      fuel truck is used first.

6.3.3 Call Altamaha for the next delivery to the same site at the same time, so the truck can be
      released.

6.3.4 Where two sites compete for FTK-WREN-3, the Water Incident Lead sets the order. Sites
      serving a hospital or critical facility per DOM 14.140 go first.
6.3.5 CAUTION: Do not fuel a running generator unless the unit is rated for hot refuelling.
6.4 Records of delivery
6.4.1 Driver records gallons delivered, gauge before and after, and time (24-hour EDT).
6.4.2 Vendor delivery tickets are scanned to the F-MAL-022 record within 12 h.

blocks: 2.0 SCOPE

It applies to diesel standby generators at SGW booster and pump stations in South Carolina and
Georgia. Covered units include GEN-PS38-COPPERLEAF and GEN-PS52-DEERWATER; the full list is in
Attachment A.

It does not apply to portable generators. For PS-17 see WDS 03.318; for monthly load tests see
WDS 03.350.
3.0 RESPONSIBILITIES
Water Incident Lead: approves refuel priority when several stations need fuel at once.
Station Operator: reads and logs fuel level, raises refuel requests.
Water SCADA Operator: watches remote tank-level signals and alerts the Station Operator.
Logistics Section Chief: assigns the vendor or the SGW fuel truck per MAL 05.040.
6.0 PROCEDURE
6.1 Start of Run

6.1.1 When a unit starts on loss of grid supply, record the start time and fuel level on
      F-WDS-207.
6.1.2 Report the start to the Water Incident Lead.
6.1.3 Calculate run time remaining using the Attachment A burn rate.
6.2 Monitoring
6.2.1 Read and log the fuel level every 4 h on F-WDS-207 while the generator runs.

6.2.2 Read the sight gauge, not only the SCADA signal. Record both if they differ by more than 5
      percent.
6.2.3 Log load (kW), oil pressure and coolant temperature with each fuel reading.

NOTE: At unmanned stations a roving operator may cover up to three stations. Keep the 4 h
      interval.
6.3 Refuel Request
6.3.1 When the fuel tank falls to 60 percent, raise a refuel request.

6.3.2 Submit the request on F-MAL-022 to the Logistics desk. State unit id, level, burn rate and
      route.

6.3.3 Flag any route that crosses a low-water crossing in GEP 2F.01 Attachment 2. Copperleaf
      Road (PS-38) and Deerwater Spur (PS-52) are on that list.

6.3.4 If run time remaining is shorter than the vendor delivery time, tell Logistics. Logistics
      then sends the SGW fuel truck first (MAL 05.040).
6.3.5 Log the delivery time and gallons received.
6.4 Shutdown
6.4.1 After return to grid supply, run unloaded for 5 min, then stop.
6.4.2 Top off to 95 percent within 24 h.

blocks: 1.0 PURPOSE OF THIS SUMMARY

This summary gives storm and Logistics staff the operating terms of contract MAL-CTR-0447 with
Altamaha Fuel & Lube for emergency diesel and gasoline supply. The signed contract held by
Supply Chain governs. Where this summary and the contract differ, the contract applies; report
the difference to the Logistics Section Chief.
2.0 PARTIES AND TERM

+--------------------+----------------------------------------------------------+
| Item               | Term                                                     |
+====================+==========================================================+
| Contract number    | MAL-CTR-0447                                             |
| Vendor             | Altamaha Fuel & Lube                                     |
| SGW contract owner | Logistics Section Chief; Manager, Supply Chain           |
| Term               | 2022-04-01 to 2027-03-31, with one 2-year renewal option |
| Amendments         | Amendment 1, signed 2024-06-24                           |
| Service area       | All SGW districts in South Carolina and Georgia          |
+--------------------+----------------------------------------------------------+
5.0 DECLARED-EVENT PROVISIONS

5.1 SGW notifies the vendor when GEP 00.010 is activated. The vendor then staffs its 24 h
    dispatch line for SGW.

5.2 The vendor reserves for SGW at least 6,000 gal per day of dyed diesel and two tank wagons
    for the first 5 days of a declared event.

5.3 The vendor shall not drive tank wagons through water over a roadway. Road closures reported
    by the driver go to SGW Logistics, who records them on F-MAL-030.

5.4 Where a delivery route crosses a low-water crossing listed in GEP 2F.01 Attachment 2, such
    as Copperleaf Road to PS-38 or Deerwater Spur to PS-52, SGW may order a pre-delivery at
    least 24 h before the forecast flooding. Pre-delivery orders count as declared-event calls.

5.5 Vendor drivers report to the staging yard gate log on arrival. They are not badged under MAL
    05.060 unless they work on SGW facilities.

5.6 Force majeure does not excuse delay caused by the vendor's own staffing. It does excuse
    delay from road closures ordered by public authority. The vendor reports any expected delay
    to SGW Logistics as soon as known.

blocks: 1.0 PURPOSE

This procedure sets how a portable bypass pump is placed and run when a sanitary lift station
cannot pump, so that the wet well does not overflow.
2.0 SCOPE

Applies to SGW wastewater lift stations in all SC and GA districts. Does not apply to treatment
plant influent pumping.
3.0 RESPONSIBILITIES

3.1 Water Incident Lead: orders bypass at any station during a declared event; sets the priority
    among stations when bypass pumps are short.
3.2 Collections Supervisor: places and runs the bypass; posts a watch.

3.3 Water Compliance Officer: decides whether an overflow is reportable and reports it per WQC
    07.150.
6.0 PROCEDURE
6.1 Assessment
6.1.1 Confirm the station alarm on SCADA. If SCADA is lost, follow WDS 03.115.
6.1.2 Determine the cause: grid outage, pump failure, control failure or flooding.
6.1.3 Read the time to overflow from Attachment A. Report it to the Water Incident Lead.
6.2 Bypass setup
6.2.1 Select a pump from Attachment B sized for the station's peak wet-weather flow.
6.2.2 Place the pump on level ground clear of traffic. Set cones and signs.

6.2.3 Run suction hose through the wet well hatch. Keep the foot valve at least 18 in. above the
      invert.

6.2.4 Connect discharge to the bypass connection on the force main. If none exists, discharge to
      the next downstream manhole.
6.2.5 Pressure test the discharge hose at operating pressure for 5 min. Inspect every joint.
6.2.6 Set the float controls: pump on at 60 percent, off at 25 percent.

6.2.7 Do a dry-run check: confirm the low-level float stops the pump before air enters the
      suction.
6.2.8 Start the pump. Confirm level falls.
6.3 Operation
6.3.1 Keep a person on watch at any bypass running without a level float.

6.3.2 Check fuel, hose joints and wet well level every 2 h. Log each check in the station log
      book.
6.3.3 Report any spill, however small, to the Water Compliance Officer at once.
6.4 Removal
6.4.1 Restore the station pumps and run two full cycles.

blocks: 1.0 PURPOSE

This procedure sets how the onsite standby generator at BPS-46 Tanyard Branch Booster is
started, loaded, watched and returned to standby when grid supply is lost.
2.0 SCOPE

Applies to BPS-46 Tanyard Branch Booster, Richmond district, Georgia. Does not apply to PS-17,
which has no onsite generator (see WDS 03.318).
3.0 RESPONSIBILITIES

3.1 Water Incident Lead: directs station start-up and shutdown during declared events; approves
    any manual transfer.

3.2 Station Operator (Richmond pump crew): performs the steps in section 6 and keeps the run
    log.

3.3 Water Control Room Operator: watches station status, zone pressure and tank level on SCADA;
    calls the Station Operator on any alarm.
3.4 Logistics Section Chief: arranges fuel on request under MAL 05.040.
6.0 PROCEDURE
6.1 Automatic start on loss of grid supply
6.1.1 Confirm on SCADA that the ATS transferred within 15 s of utility loss.
6.1.2 Confirm pumps 1 and 2 restarted on the lead-lag sequence. Allow 45 s stagger.
6.1.3 Log start time, kW and fuel level on F-WDS-207.

6.1.4 Notify the Water Incident Lead by phone. During business hours also notify the Richmond
      district supervisor.
6.1.5 Dispatch the Station Operator to site within 2 h to verify local readings.
6.2 Run-time monitoring

6.2.1 Read the fuel gauge and log kW, coolant temperature and oil pressure every 4 h on
      F-WDS-207.
6.2.2 Raise the refuel request at the tank level set in WDS 03.322. Use F-MAL-022.

6.2.3 Compare remaining run time against vendor delivery time. If remaining run time is shorter,
      ask Logistics for the SGW fuel truck first (MAL 05.040).
6.2.4 Record any alarm, shutdown or restart with the time in 24-hour format.
6.3 Failure of automatic transfer
NOTE: Use this subsection only on the Water Incident Lead's order.
6.3.1 Confirm the generator is running at rated voltage and frequency.
6.3.2 Place the ATS controller in OFF.
6.3.3 Operate the manual bypass handle to EMERGENCY. Observe the position flag.
6.3.4 Start pump 1 locally. Wait 60 s. Start pump 2.
6.3.5 Report the manual transfer to the Water Control Room Operator and log it.
6.4 Return to grid supply
