blocks: 2.0 SCOPE

Onsite diesel standby generators at water and wastewater facilities. Portable generators such as
MGEN-HALBERD-500 are tested under MAL 05.040.
3.0 RESPONSIBILITIES
3.1 Station Operator: runs the test and fills the test record.
3.2 Generator Maintenance Technician: corrects defects found.

3.3 Water Control Room Operator: is told before and after each test, because the test transfers
    station load.
4.0 PRECAUTIONS AND LIMITS
4.1 Test under station load through the ATS where one is fitted. A no-load run does not count.

4.2 Load shall reach at least 30 percent of nameplate kW for 30 min, or the exhaust temperature
    shall reach the manufacturer's minimum.

4.3 No test when a tropical storm watch or warning covers the district. Generator readiness
    checks then follow the GEP 2H.01 phase table.
4.4 CAUTION: Hearing protection is required inside the enclosure.
5.0 PROCEDURE
5.1 Call the Water Control Room. Give station, generator id and planned start time.
5.2 Walk down the unit: oil, coolant, belts, battery terminals, fuel leaks, louvers clear.
5.3 Read the fuel gauge. Record it.
5.4 Simulate utility loss at the ATS test switch.
5.5 Confirm transfer within 15 s. Record the time to transfer.

5.6 Run under load for 30 min. Record kW, volts, amps, frequency, oil pressure and coolant
    temperature at 0, 15 and 30 min.
5.7 End the test. Confirm retransfer and the 5 min cooldown.
5.8 Read the fuel gauge again.

5.9 From June 1 to November 30 keep the sub-base tank at or above 90 percent after the test.
    Request fuel on F-MAL-022 if lower.
5.10 Return the unit to AUTO. Call the Water Control Room.

blocks: 1.0 PURPOSE

This procedure sets how a portable bypass pump is placed and run when a sanitary lift station
cannot pump, so that the wet well does not overflow.
2.0 SCOPE

Applies to SGW wastewater lift stations in all SC and GA districts. Does not apply to treatment
plant influent pumping.
3.0 RESPONSIBILITIES

3.1 Water Incident Lead: orders bypass at any station during a declared event; sets the priority
    among stations when bypass pumps are short.
3.2 Collections Supervisor: places and runs the bypass; posts a watch.

3.3 Water Compliance Officer: decides whether an overflow is reportable and reports it per WQC
    07.150.
6.0 PROCEDURE
6.1 Assessment
6.1.1 Confirm the station alarm on SCADA. If SCADA is lost, follow WDS 03.115.
6.1.2 Determine the cause: grid outage, pump failure, control failure or flooding.
6.1.3 Read the time to overflow from Attachment A. Report it to the Water Incident Lead.
6.2 Bypass setup
6.2.1 Select a pump from Attachment B sized for the station's peak wet-weather flow.
6.2.2 Place the pump on level ground clear of traffic. Set cones and signs.

6.2.3 Run suction hose through the wet well hatch. Keep the foot valve at least 18 in. above the
      invert.

6.2.4 Connect discharge to the bypass connection on the force main. If none exists, discharge to
      the next downstream manhole.
6.2.5 Pressure test the discharge hose at operating pressure for 5 min. Inspect every joint.
6.2.6 Set the float controls: pump on at 60 percent, off at 25 percent.

6.2.7 Do a dry-run check: confirm the low-level float stops the pump before air enters the
      suction.
6.2.8 Start the pump. Confirm level falls.
6.3 Operation
6.3.1 Keep a person on watch at any bypass running without a level float.

6.3.2 Check fuel, hose joints and wet well level every 2 h. Log each check in the station log
      book.
6.3.3 Report any spill, however small, to the Water Compliance Officer at once.
6.4 Removal
6.4.1 Restore the station pumps and run two full cycles.

blocks: 2.0 SCOPE

Onsite diesel standby generators at water and wastewater facilities. Portable generators such as
MGEN-HALBERD-500 are tested under MAL 05.040.
3.0 RESPONSIBILITIES
3.1 Station Operator: runs the test and fills the test record.
3.2 Generator Maintenance Technician: corrects defects found.

3.3 Water Control Room Operator: is told before and after each test, because the test transfers
    station load.
4.0 PRECAUTIONS AND LIMITS
4.1 Test under station load through the ATS where one is fitted. A no-load run does not count.

4.2 Load shall reach at least 30 percent of nameplate kW for 30 min, or the exhaust temperature
    shall reach the manufacturer's minimum.

4.3 No test when a tropical storm watch or warning covers the district. Generator readiness
    checks then follow the GEP 2H.01 phase table.
4.4 CAUTION: Hearing protection is required inside the enclosure.
5.0 PROCEDURE
5.1 Call the Water Control Room. Give station, generator id and planned start time.
5.2 Walk down the unit: oil, coolant, belts, battery terminals, fuel leaks, louvers clear.
5.3 Read the fuel gauge. Record it.
5.4 Simulate utility loss at the ATS test switch.
5.5 Confirm transfer within 15 s. Record the time to transfer.

5.6 Run under load for 30 min. Record kW, volts, amps, frequency, oil pressure and coolant
    temperature at 0, 15 and 30 min.
5.7 End the test. Confirm retransfer and the 5 min cooldown.
5.8 Read the fuel gauge again.

5.9 From June 1 to November 30 keep the sub-base tank at or above 90 percent after the test.
    Request fuel on F-MAL-022 if lower.
5.10 Return the unit to AUTO. Call the Water Control Room.

blocks: 1.0 PURPOSE

This procedure sets how the onsite standby generator at BPS-46 Tanyard Branch Booster is
started, loaded, watched and returned to standby when grid supply is lost.
2.0 SCOPE

Applies to BPS-46 Tanyard Branch Booster, Richmond district, Georgia. Does not apply to PS-17,
which has no onsite generator (see WDS 03.318).
3.0 RESPONSIBILITIES

3.1 Water Incident Lead: directs station start-up and shutdown during declared events; approves
    any manual transfer.

3.2 Station Operator (Richmond pump crew): performs the steps in section 6 and keeps the run
    log.

3.3 Water Control Room Operator: watches station status, zone pressure and tank level on SCADA;
    calls the Station Operator on any alarm.
3.4 Logistics Section Chief: arranges fuel on request under MAL 05.040.
6.0 PROCEDURE
6.1 Automatic start on loss of grid supply
6.1.1 Confirm on SCADA that the ATS transferred within 15 s of utility loss.
6.1.2 Confirm pumps 1 and 2 restarted on the lead-lag sequence. Allow 45 s stagger.
6.1.3 Log start time, kW and fuel level on F-WDS-207.

6.1.4 Notify the Water Incident Lead by phone. During business hours also notify the Richmond
      district supervisor.
6.1.5 Dispatch the Station Operator to site within 2 h to verify local readings.
6.2 Run-time monitoring

6.2.1 Read the fuel gauge and log kW, coolant temperature and oil pressure every 4 h on
      F-WDS-207.
6.2.2 Raise the refuel request at the tank level set in WDS 03.322. Use F-MAL-022.

6.2.3 Compare remaining run time against vendor delivery time. If remaining run time is shorter,
      ask Logistics for the SGW fuel truck first (MAL 05.040).
6.2.4 Record any alarm, shutdown or restart with the time in 24-hour format.
6.3 Failure of automatic transfer
NOTE: Use this subsection only on the Water Incident Lead's order.
6.3.1 Confirm the generator is running at rated voltage and frequency.
6.3.2 Place the ATS controller in OFF.
6.3.3 Operate the manual bypass handle to EMERGENCY. Observe the position flag.
6.3.4 Start pump 1 locally. Wait 60 s. Start pump 2.
6.3.5 Report the manual transfer to the Water Control Room Operator and log it.
6.4 Return to grid supply

blocks: 1.0 PURPOSE

This procedure sets how SGW records, reports and gives public notice of sanitary sewer overflows
(SSOs) in South Carolina and Georgia.
2.0 SCOPE

All SGW wastewater collection systems and lift stations. Plant bypasses are reported under the
plant's NPDES permit procedure.
3.0 RESPONSIBILITIES

3.1 Collections Supervisor: reports every overflow to the Water Compliance Officer as soon as
    found; estimates volume.

3.2 Water Compliance Officer: decides reportability, makes the agency reports and approves
    public notice.
3.3 Director, Corporate Communications: issues news releases when Attachment A requires one.
6.0 PROCEDURE
6.1 Field report

6.1.1 Note start time, location, cause and whether the overflow reached a stream, ditch or storm
      inlet.
6.1.2 Photograph the site.
6.1.3 Call the Water Compliance Officer. After hours, call the compliance on-call phone.
6.2 Volume
6.2.1 Estimate volume by Attachment B. Record the method.
6.2.2 Update the estimate when the overflow stops.
6.3 Agency reports
6.3.1 Report by phone or the agency portal within 24 h of becoming aware of the overflow.

6.3.2 South Carolina: report to SCDES Region staff; written report within 5 days (SC
      R.61-9.122.41(l)(6)).

6.3.3 Georgia: report to the Georgia EPD district office; follow Ga. Comp. R. & Regs.
      391-3-6-.05 for public notice and follow-up.
6.4 Public notice
6.4.1 Post signs at the overflow site and where the release entered state waters.

6.4.2 Where Attachment A requires it, notify the county health department and issue a news
      release within 24 h.

6.4.3 Georgia spills of 10,000 gal or more that reach state waters also need a legal notice in
      the county organ and stream monitoring. The Water Compliance Officer sets the monitoring
      points.
6.5 During declared storm events
6.5.1 Many overflows may occur during one event. Keep one SSO log per district.
6.5.2 With the agency's agreement, report overflows of one event once per day on the log.

6.5.3 Overflows that reach a drinking-water intake reach are reported at once regardless of
      batching.

blocks: 2.0 SCOPE

All SGW potable-water pressure zones in South Carolina and Georgia. It does not apply to
raw-water mains or to fire-line testing.
3.0 RESPONSIBILITIES
Water SCADA Operator: acknowledges pressure alarms and starts section 6.
Water Distribution Supervisor (on call): sends a crew to verify the reading in the field.
Water Incident Lead: directs station, tank and generator actions during an event.

Water Compliance Officer: decides, with the Water Incident Lead, whether a boil water advisory
or notice is issued.
6.0 PROCEDURE
6.1 Alarm
6.1.1 Acknowledge the alarm within 5 min.
6.1.2 Check station status, tank level and any active main break in the zone.
6.1.3 Trend the zone critical point for the past 2 h.
6.2 Field Verification
6.2.1 Send the on-call crew with a calibrated gauge.
6.2.2 Read at the hydrant nearest the critical point. Record the reading, time and hydrant id.
6.2.3 For zones fed by a booster on generator power, read at the station discharge too.
6.3 Restore Pressure
6.3.1 Start standby pumps if available.

6.3.2 If the station has lost power, follow WDS 03.322 (fixed generator) or WDS 03.318 (PS-17
      portable hookup).
6.3.3 Track tank drawdown per WDS 03.240.
6.3.4 Notify critical customers in the zone using DOM 14.140.
6.4 Below the State Minimum

6.4.1 When pressure at a service connection falls below the state minimum, notify the Water
      Compliance Officer within 1 h.

6.4.2 The Water Compliance Officer starts the boil water evaluation under WQC 07.114 (Georgia)
      or WQC 07.120 (South Carolina).

6.4.3 Record the affected streets and zones on the advisory map. Use the zone ids from
      Attachment A.
6.4.4 Keep reading the critical point every 30 min until pressure is above the minimum for 2 h.

CAUTION: Do not start flushing before the boil water decision is made. Flushing can pull
         pressure lower.
6.4.5 Hand the readings to the Water Compliance Officer for the regulator report.

blocks: 4.0 DEFINITIONS
Global ETR: the time by which 90 percent of affected customers are restored, system-wide.
Regional ETR: the same 90 percent measure for one operating region.
P25, P50, P75: the 25th, 50th and 75th percentiles of the modelled 90 percent restoration time.
All-clear: as defined in GEP 2H.01 section 3.0.
5.0 PRECAUTIONS AND LIMITS
5.1 Do not release an ETR that has not been approved per 6.2.4.
5.2 Model runs use crew counts on property or confirmed en route, not requested crews.
5.3 A model run older than 6 h shall not be used for release.
6.0 PROCEDURE
6.1 Before All-Clear
6.1.1 Run the pre-landfall model at each NHC advisory once the Event Type is 1 or 2.
6.1.2 Share the run with the Duty Manager for staffing decisions. Do not publish it.
6.2 Global ETR
6.2.1 Publish the global ETR within 24 h after the all-clear.

6.2.2 State the global ETR as a range: P25, P50 and P75 (range of the 25th, 50th and 75th
      percentiles).
6.2.3 The ETR Specialist proposes the global ETR on F-DOM-121 with the model inputs attached.

6.2.4 The Incident Commander and the Duty Manager approve the global ETR before release. Both
      signatures go on F-DOM-121.

6.2.5 Send the approved range to the Public Information Officer. Release wording follows PCN
      02.044.
NOTE: The P50 is the headline time in media statements. P25 and P75 are given as the range.
6.3 Regional ETRs

6.3.1 Regional ETRs follow once damage assessment has patrolled 80 percent of circuits in the
      region.

6.3.2 Use the patrol completion count from the Damage Assessment Coordinator, not crew
      estimates.
6.3.3 Approve and release regional ETRs as in 6.2.3 to 6.2.5.
6.4 Revision
6.4.1 Re-run the model at each operational period change.
6.4.2 Revise a published ETR when the P50 moves by more than 12 h.
6.4.3 A move of 12 h or less is logged but not released.
6.4.4 Revised ETRs need the same approvals as in 6.2.4.

This template gives the wording and approval path for the public release of SGW's global
estimated time of restoration (ETR) during Event Types 1 to 3.

Applies to system-wide and district-level global ETR releases on sgw web outage pages, social
channels, media advisories and the IVR storm message. Does not apply to routine single-feeder

    earliest and a latest time), never as a single time. Take the earliest and latest bounds

blocks: 4.0 DEMOBILIZATION
4.1 Trigger

The Planning Section Chief starts the Demobilization Plan when the remaining outage count has
fallen below

25 percent of the peak, or earlier when the IC directs. Release is never planned before the
global ETR has been published under DOM 14.206.
4.2 Release Order
Release resources in this order unless the IC directs otherwise:
a. Mutual-aid crews from the farthest home utility first.
b. Contract vegetation and line crews.
c. Mutual-aid crews from nearer utilities.
d. Native crews borrowed between districts.
e. Damage assessors, then wire guards.
4.3 Release Steps

4.3.1 The Duty Manager lists the crews that can be released, by district, at the planning
      meeting.

4.3.2 The Planning Section Chief adds them to the Demobilization Plan with a release date and
      time (EDT).
4.3.3 The IC approves the plan.

4.3.4 The Logistics Section Chief notifies SEE of mutual-aid releases through the channel used
      for the request (MAL 05.012).
4.3.5 Crews return SGW material, radios and badges at the yard. Check-out follows MAL 05.060.

4.3.6 The Safety Officer confirms each released crew has had the rest period in DOM 12.050
      before travel.

4.3.7 Logistics closes lodging and meal orders per MAL 05.030 within 24 h of the last crew
      leaving.

4.3.8 Logistics closes each staging yard when the last crew has left and the site is restored
      per MAL 05.020.

CAUTION: do not release a crew that holds a clearance or a Hot Line Hold. The clearance is
         returned under TSO

blocks: 4.0 DEFINITIONS AND ABBREVIATIONS
Service connection: the point where the customer service line meets the SGW main.
Heavy flow: fire flow, main flushing or a main break draining the zone.
Low-pressure event: any verified reading below the state minimum in 5.1 or 5.2.
5.0 PRECAUTIONS AND LIMITS

5.1 South Carolina systems: minimum 25 psi at service connections in normal operation, and 20
    psi under heavy flow (SC R.61-58.7.E(7)).
5.2 Georgia systems: minimum 20 psi at all times (Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. 391-3-5-.10).

5.3 The SCADA low-pressure alarm is set at 40 psi at every zone critical point. Do not lower it
    without Water Incident Lead approval.
5.4 The high-pressure alarm is 110 psi. Above 120 psi, isolate the PRV station.

5.5 A SCADA reading alone is not a verified low-pressure event. Confirm it with a field gauge or
    a second sensor.
6.0 PROCEDURE
6.1 Alarm
6.1.1 Acknowledge the alarm within 5 min.
6.1.2 Check station status, tank level and any active main break in the zone.
6.1.3 Trend the zone critical point for the past 2 h.
6.2 Field Verification
6.2.1 Send the on-call crew with a calibrated gauge.
6.2.2 Read at the hydrant nearest the critical point. Record the reading, time and hydrant id.
6.2.3 For zones fed by a booster on generator power, read at the station discharge too.
6.3 Restore Pressure
6.3.1 Start standby pumps if available.

6.3.2 If the station has lost power, follow WDS 03.322 (fixed generator) or WDS 03.318 (PS-17
      portable hookup).
6.3.3 Track tank drawdown per WDS 03.240.
6.3.4 Notify critical customers in the zone using DOM 14.140.
6.4 Below the State Minimum

6.4.1 When pressure at a service connection falls below the state minimum, notify the Water
      Compliance Officer within 1 h.

6.4.2 The Water Compliance Officer starts the boil water evaluation under WQC 07.114 (Georgia)
      or WQC 07.120 (South Carolina).

6.4.3 Record the affected streets and zones on the advisory map. Use the zone ids from
      Attachment A.
6.4.4 Keep reading the critical point every 30 min until pressure is above the minimum for 2 h.

CAUTION: Do not start flushing before the boil water decision is made. Flushing can pull
         pressure lower.
6.4.5 Hand the readings to the Water Compliance Officer for the regulator report.

blocks: 5.0 CREW SAFETY
5.1 Lightning
5.1.1 Stop work at a structure when lightning is within 10 mi or thunder is heard.
5.1.2 Resume 30 min after the last lightning within 10 mi.

5.1.3 Aerial-lift work stops when sustained wind exceeds 30 mph (DOM 14.110). Gusts in
      thunderstorm outflow often exceed this before the rain arrives.
5.2 Tornado Warning

5.2.1 The Distribution Control Center broadcasts each NWS Tornado Warning on the district
      talkgroups within
2 min of issue.
5.2.2 Crews inside or within 5 mi of the warning polygon shall stop work and shelter.

5.2.3 Shelter in a sturdy building, interior room, lowest floor. A vehicle is not shelter. If no
      building is reachable, leave the truck and lie flat in the lowest ground away from poles
      and trees.
5.2.4 Crews report "sheltered" and "clear" by radio. The Duty Manager logs both times.

5.2.5 Crews resume work only after the warning expires and the supervisor has checked the site
      for new downed wires.

Public messaging follows PCN 02.050. Corporate Communications releases a downed-wire safety
message within
1 h of a confirmed tornado touchdown in the service area.

This procedure sets how the onsite standby generator at BPS-46 Tanyard Branch Booster is
started, loaded, watched and returned to standby when grid supply is lost.
2.0 SCOPE

Applies to BPS-46 Tanyard Branch Booster, Richmond district, Georgia. Does not apply to PS-17,
which has no onsite generator (see WDS 03.318).
3.0 RESPONSIBILITIES

3.1 Water Incident Lead: directs station start-up and shutdown during declared events; approves
    any manual transfer.

3.2 Station Operator (Richmond pump crew): performs the steps in section 6 and keeps the run
    log.

3.3 Water Control Room Operator: watches station status, zone pressure and tank level on SCADA;
    calls the Station Operator on any alarm.
3.4 Logistics Section Chief: arranges fuel on request under MAL 05.040.
6.0 PROCEDURE
6.1 Automatic start on loss of grid supply
6.1.1 Confirm on SCADA that the ATS transferred within 15 s of utility loss.
6.1.2 Confirm pumps 1 and 2 restarted on the lead-lag sequence. Allow 45 s stagger.
6.1.3 Log start time, kW and fuel level on F-WDS-207.

6.1.4 Notify the Water Incident Lead by phone. During business hours also notify the Richmond
      district supervisor.
6.1.5 Dispatch the Station Operator to site within 2 h to verify local readings.
6.2 Run-time monitoring

6.2.1 Read the fuel gauge and log kW, coolant temperature and oil pressure every 4 h on
      F-WDS-207.
6.2.2 Raise the refuel request at the tank level set in WDS 03.322. Use F-MAL-022.

6.2.3 Compare remaining run time against vendor delivery time. If remaining run time is shorter,
      ask Logistics for the SGW fuel truck first (MAL 05.040).
6.2.4 Record any alarm, shutdown or restart with the time in 24-hour format.
6.3 Failure of automatic transfer
NOTE: Use this subsection only on the Water Incident Lead's order.
6.3.1 Confirm the generator is running at rated voltage and frequency.
6.3.2 Place the ATS controller in OFF.
6.3.3 Operate the manual bypass handle to EMERGENCY. Observe the position flag.
6.3.4 Start pump 1 locally. Wait 60 s. Start pump 2.
6.3.5 Report the manual transfer to the Water Control Room Operator and log it.
6.4 Return to grid supply

blocks: 6.0 PROCEDURE
6.1 Assessment
6.1.1 Confirm the station alarm on SCADA. If SCADA is lost, follow WDS 03.115.
6.1.2 Determine the cause: grid outage, pump failure, control failure or flooding.
6.1.3 Read the time to overflow from Attachment A. Report it to the Water Incident Lead.
6.2 Bypass setup
6.2.1 Select a pump from Attachment B sized for the station's peak wet-weather flow.
6.2.2 Place the pump on level ground clear of traffic. Set cones and signs.

6.2.3 Run suction hose through the wet well hatch. Keep the foot valve at least 18 in. above the
      invert.

6.2.4 Connect discharge to the bypass connection on the force main. If none exists, discharge to
      the next downstream manhole.
6.2.5 Pressure test the discharge hose at operating pressure for 5 min. Inspect every joint.
6.2.6 Set the float controls: pump on at 60 percent, off at 25 percent.

6.2.7 Do a dry-run check: confirm the low-level float stops the pump before air enters the
      suction.
6.2.8 Start the pump. Confirm level falls.
6.3 Operation
6.3.1 Keep a person on watch at any bypass running without a level float.

6.3.2 Check fuel, hose joints and wet well level every 2 h. Log each check in the station log
      book.
6.3.3 Report any spill, however small, to the Water Compliance Officer at once.
6.4 Removal
6.4.1 Restore the station pumps and run two full cycles.
6.0 PROCEDURE
6.4.1 Restore the station pumps and run two full cycles.
6.4.2 Stop the bypass. Drain hoses to the wet well.
6.4.3 Remove equipment and clean the site.

blocks: 6.0 PROCEDURE
6.1 Before All-Clear
6.1.1 Run the pre-landfall model at each NHC advisory once the Event Type is 1 or 2.
6.1.2 Share the run with the Duty Manager for staffing decisions. Do not publish it.
6.2 Global ETR
6.2.1 Publish the global ETR within 24 h after the all-clear.

6.2.2 State the global ETR as a range: P25, P50 and P75 (range of the 25th, 50th and 75th
      percentiles).
6.2.3 The ETR Specialist proposes the global ETR on F-DOM-121 with the model inputs attached.

6.2.4 The Incident Commander and the Duty Manager approve the global ETR before release. Both
      signatures go on F-DOM-121.

6.2.5 Send the approved range to the Public Information Officer. Release wording follows PCN
      02.044.
NOTE: The P50 is the headline time in media statements. P25 and P75 are given as the range.
6.3 Regional ETRs

6.3.1 Regional ETRs follow once damage assessment has patrolled 80 percent of circuits in the
      region.

6.3.2 Use the patrol completion count from the Damage Assessment Coordinator, not crew
      estimates.
6.3.3 Approve and release regional ETRs as in 6.2.3 to 6.2.5.
6.4 Revision
6.4.1 Re-run the model at each operational period change.
6.4.2 Revise a published ETR when the P50 moves by more than 12 h.
6.4.3 A move of 12 h or less is logged but not released.
6.4.4 Revised ETRs need the same approvals as in 6.2.4.

3.0 POSITION DESCRIPTIONS
3.1 Incident Commander
a. Sets the Event Type and Activation Level per GEP 00.010.
b. Approves incident objectives on the ICS 202 for each operational period.

c. Approves crew pre-positioning plans and mutual-aid requests jointly with the Logistics
   Section Chief.
d. Approves the global ETR with the Duty Manager per DOM 14.206.
e. Approves cross-domain priority decisions with the Water Incident Lead per DOM 14.215.
3.2 Duty Manager (Electric Operations)

The Duty Manager (Electric Operations) leads the storm room for distribution restoration. The
position is filled from the Duty Manager pool led by the Director, Distribution Operations.
a. Proposes the Event Type and crew staging plans to the Incident Commander.
b. Directs crew assignments by district through the Operations Section.

c. Re-balances crews between staging yards inside the approved tolerance band (GEP 2H.01 section
   6.4).
d. Co-approves the global ETR before release.
e. Hands over at shift change per DOM 14.105.
3.3 Operations Section Chief

Supervises the Electric Branch and the Water Branch. In a Type 3 or Type 4 event the Duty
Manager may also fill this position.
3.4 Planning Section Chief

Runs the planning cycle, prepares the IAP and maintains situation status. Issues the situation
reports.
3.5 ETR Specialist

The ETR Specialist sits in the Planning Section and proposes the global ETR. The specialist also
proposes regional ETRs once the patrol threshold in DOM 14.206 section 6.3 is met.

1.0 PURPOSE

This section sets how the SGW Emergency Operations Center (EOC) is opened, staffed and
connected, and how activation is announced. Activation Levels are defined in GEP 00.010 section
5.
4.0 ACTIVATION
4.1 Activation Steps
4.1.1 The IC decides the Activation Level and the Event Type and records both on F-GEP-012.

4.1.2 The EOC Manager sends the activation message on the mass notification system within 15 min
      of the IC decision. The message states the Activation Level, the Event Type, the first
      briefing time (EDT) and the EOC location.

4.1.3 Positions on the notification list shall acknowledge within 30 min. The EOC Manager calls
      each position that has not acknowledged, then its alternate.

4.1.4 At Level 3 or higher, the EOC Manager opens the physical EOC and confirms power, data and
      HVAC.

4.1.5 At Level 2 or higher, the IC sets the operational period, normally 12 h (0700 to 1900 and
      1900 to

4.1.6 The Planning Section Chief schedules the first planning meeting no later than 4 h after
      activation.
4.1.7 The Liaison Officer contacts county EOCs from Level 2 (see GEP 00.010 section 5.3.3).

NOTE: a water-only event may open the EOC at Level 3 with the Water Incident Lead seated and the
      electric desks on call.
4.2 Alternate EOC

Move to the alternate EOC when the primary has lost power and generator supply, has lost both
data paths, or is inside a mandatory evacuation zone. The move shall be complete within 6 h of
the IC decision. The virtual EOC on the conference bridge carries command during the move.

blocks: 4.0 DEFINITIONS AND ABBREVIATIONS
Service connection: the point where the customer service line meets the SGW main.
Heavy flow: fire flow, main flushing or a main break draining the zone.
Low-pressure event: any verified reading below the state minimum in 5.1 or 5.2.
5.0 PRECAUTIONS AND LIMITS

5.1 South Carolina systems: minimum 25 psi at service connections in normal operation, and 20
    psi under heavy flow (SC R.61-58.7.E(7)).
5.2 Georgia systems: minimum 20 psi at all times (Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. 391-3-5-.10).

5.3 The SCADA low-pressure alarm is set at 40 psi at every zone critical point. Do not lower it
    without Water Incident Lead approval.
5.4 The high-pressure alarm is 110 psi. Above 120 psi, isolate the PRV station.

5.5 A SCADA reading alone is not a verified low-pressure event. Confirm it with a field gauge or
    a second sensor.

blocks: 6.0 PROCEDURE
6.1 Plan
6.1.1 Get the pre-outage load for the same hour from SCADA history.
6.1.2 Apply the CLPU factor from Attachment A.

6.1.3 Divide the feeder into pickup steps using sectionalizing switches, reclosers and fused
      laterals.

6.1.4 Order the steps so critical facilities flagged in the DOM 14.140 registry are in the first
      step where the switching allows (priority per DOM 14.215).
6.1.5 Write the steps on the switching order.
6.2 Execute
6.2.1 Open all downstream sectionalizing points before closing the feeder breaker.
6.2.2 Close the breaker with the first step only.
6.2.3 Read feeder current at 1 min and 5 min.
6.2.4 Close the next step when 5.3 is met.
6.2.5 Repeat to the last step.
6.2.6 Return relay settings and reclosing to normal and record the time.
6.3 Trips during Pickup
6.3.1 If the breaker trips on the first step, patrol for a fault before any reclose.
6.3.2 If it trips on a later step with no fault found, split that step in two and retry.
6.3.3 After two trips on the same step with no fault found, call the Duty Manager.
7.0 RECORDS
Switching orders, SCADA load trend for the pickup, trip reports. Retain 3 years.
8.0 REFERENCES
ATTACHMENT A - CLPU Factors

Factors apply to residential-dominated feeders. Use 1.3 for feeders with more than 60 percent
commercial load.

blocks: 2.0 SCOPE

Applies when the NWS issues a Winter Storm Watch, Winter Storm Warning or Ice Storm Warning for
any county in the service area, or a Hard Freeze Warning with temperatures below 20 F for 6 h or
more.
3.0 HAZARD SUMMARY

Ice accretion breaks limbs and conductors over wide areas, and damage keeps growing for hours
after precipitation stops. Road access is the limiting factor for crews and fuel. Hard freezes
cause service line and main breaks; demand rises when customers drip faucets, and tanks drain
overnight.
7.0 WATER OPERATIONS

7.1 Pump stations shall keep enclosure temperature above 40 F. Portable heaters are on generator
    power where grid supply is lost.
7.2 Main breaks are handled per WDS 03.410. Isolation follows WDS 03.240.
7.3 Track elevated tank levels every 2 h overnight during a hard freeze (WDS 03.205).

7.4 When pressure falls below the state minimum, follow WDS 03.105 and notify the Water
    Compliance Officer.
8.0 LOGISTICS

8.1 Chained or four-wheel-drive vehicles are assigned to fuel runs. FTK-WREN-3 carries chains
    from 1 December to 15 March.

blocks: 4.0 DEFINITIONS AND ABBREVIATIONS
Service connection: the point where the customer service line meets the SGW main.
Heavy flow: fire flow, main flushing or a main break draining the zone.
Low-pressure event: any verified reading below the state minimum in 5.1 or 5.2.
5.0 PRECAUTIONS AND LIMITS

5.1 South Carolina systems: minimum 25 psi at service connections in normal operation, and 20
    psi under heavy flow (SC R.61-58.7.E(7)).
5.2 Georgia systems: minimum 20 psi at all times (Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. 391-3-5-.10).

5.3 The SCADA low-pressure alarm is set at 40 psi at every zone critical point. Do not lower it
    without Water Incident Lead approval.
5.4 The high-pressure alarm is 110 psi. Above 120 psi, isolate the PRV station.

5.5 A SCADA reading alone is not a verified low-pressure event. Confirm it with a field gauge or
    a second sensor.
6.0 PROCEDURE
6.1 Alarm
6.1.1 Acknowledge the alarm within 5 min.
6.1.2 Check station status, tank level and any active main break in the zone.
6.1.3 Trend the zone critical point for the past 2 h.
6.2 Field Verification
6.2.1 Send the on-call crew with a calibrated gauge.
6.2.2 Read at the hydrant nearest the critical point. Record the reading, time and hydrant id.
6.2.3 For zones fed by a booster on generator power, read at the station discharge too.
6.3 Restore Pressure
6.3.1 Start standby pumps if available.

6.3.2 If the station has lost power, follow WDS 03.322 (fixed generator) or WDS 03.318 (PS-17
      portable hookup).
6.3.3 Track tank drawdown per WDS 03.240.
6.3.4 Notify critical customers in the zone using DOM 14.140.
6.4 Below the State Minimum

6.4.1 When pressure at a service connection falls below the state minimum, notify the Water
      Compliance Officer within 1 h.

6.4.2 The Water Compliance Officer starts the boil water evaluation under WQC 07.114 (Georgia)
      or WQC 07.120 (South Carolina).

6.4.3 Record the affected streets and zones on the advisory map. Use the zone ids from
      Attachment A.
6.4.4 Keep reading the critical point every 30 min until pressure is above the minimum for 2 h.

CAUTION: Do not start flushing before the boil water decision is made. Flushing can pull
         pressure lower.
6.4.5 Hand the readings to the Water Compliance Officer for the regulator report.

blocks: 1.0 PURPOSE

This procedure sets how SGW records, reports and gives public notice of sanitary sewer overflows
(SSOs) in South Carolina and Georgia.
2.0 SCOPE

All SGW wastewater collection systems and lift stations. Plant bypasses are reported under the
plant's NPDES permit procedure.
3.0 RESPONSIBILITIES

3.1 Collections Supervisor: reports every overflow to the Water Compliance Officer as soon as
    found; estimates volume.

3.2 Water Compliance Officer: decides reportability, makes the agency reports and approves
    public notice.
3.3 Director, Corporate Communications: issues news releases when Attachment A requires one.
6.0 PROCEDURE
6.1 Field report

6.1.1 Note start time, location, cause and whether the overflow reached a stream, ditch or storm
      inlet.
6.1.2 Photograph the site.
6.1.3 Call the Water Compliance Officer. After hours, call the compliance on-call phone.
6.2 Volume
6.2.1 Estimate volume by Attachment B. Record the method.
6.2.2 Update the estimate when the overflow stops.
6.3 Agency reports
6.3.1 Report by phone or the agency portal within 24 h of becoming aware of the overflow.

6.3.2 South Carolina: report to SCDES Region staff; written report within 5 days (SC
      R.61-9.122.41(l)(6)).

6.3.3 Georgia: report to the Georgia EPD district office; follow Ga. Comp. R. & Regs.
      391-3-6-.05 for public notice and follow-up.
6.4 Public notice
6.4.1 Post signs at the overflow site and where the release entered state waters.

6.4.2 Where Attachment A requires it, notify the county health department and issue a news
      release within 24 h.

6.4.3 Georgia spills of 10,000 gal or more that reach state waters also need a legal notice in
      the county organ and stream monitoring. The Water Compliance Officer sets the monitoring
      points.
6.5 During declared storm events
6.5.1 Many overflows may occur during one event. Keep one SSO log per district.
6.5.2 With the agency's agreement, report overflows of one event once per day on the log.

6.5.3 Overflows that reach a drinking-water intake reach are reported at once regardless of
      batching.

blocks: 6.0 PROCEDURE
6.1 On transfer to generator
6.1.1 Confirm pumps restarted and flow is above 150 gpm.
6.1.2 Confirm the metering pump is running and its stroke counter is moving.
6.1.3 Check the calibration column. Record the draw-down rate in gal/h.
6.1.4 Take a free chlorine reading at the station discharge tap within 30 min.
6.2 Flow-paced restart sequence
6.2.1 If feed did not restart, wait until station flow is stable for 2 min.
6.2.2 Start the metering pump in HAND at 25 percent speed.
6.2.3 After 5 min, switch to AUTO (flow-paced).
6.2.4 Recheck residual after 30 min.
6.3 While on generator power
6.3.1 Read the day tank level every 4 h with the generator readings.

6.3.2 Refill the day tank at 25 percent. Do not let it run dry; air in the suction line stops
      feed.
6.3.3 Take a residual at the discharge every 8 h and at the far zone point once per day.

6.3.4 If the discharge residual is below 1.0 mg/L, raise the feed rate by 10 percent and recheck
      in 30 min.

6.3.5 If any distribution reading is below the state minimum, notify the Water Compliance
      Officer.
6.4 On return to grid supply
6.4.1 Confirm feed restarted after retransfer.
6.4.2 Take a discharge residual within 30 min.
6.4.3 Log the end of generator operation in the feed log.
7.0 RECORDS
Station feed log, kept 5 years. Residual results go to the Water Quality data system.

MTS: manual transfer switch. PS-17 has a manual transfer switch and no automatic transfer switch

Hookup lead time: time from dispatch of the portable generator to pumping on generator power.

Residual-pressure limit: tank level below which zone pressure cannot be held (WDS 03.240

5.0 PRECAUTIONS AND LIMITS

5.1 Plan on a hookup lead time of 150 min from dispatch to pumping. This covers travel, cable
    connection and manual transfer.

5.2 The station draws 412 kW at two-pump duty. MGEN-HALBERD-500 (500 kW) runs both pumps; do not
    start pump 3 on generator power.

5.3 CAUTION: The MTS is break-before-make. Open the utility-side breaker before closing the
    generator side. Backfeed onto FDR-AIK-2207 endangers line crews.
5.4 Ground the generator frame to the station ground bar before cables are landed.

5.5 Do not run the generator in the dry well. Park it on the north pad, at least 15 ft from the
    louvres.
6.0 PROCEDURE
6.3.1 Position the generator on the north pad. Chock the wheels.
6.3.2 Bond the frame to the ground bar.
6.3.3 Verify the MTS is in the OFF (centre) position.
6.3.4 Open utility breaker CB-1 and apply the station lock.

6.3.5 Land the cables at the generator connection cabinet. Check phase rotation with the
      rotation meter.
6.3.6 Start the generator. Allow 5 min warm-up at no load.
6.3.7 Move the MTS to GENERATOR.
6.3.8 Start pump 1, then pump 2 after 60 s.
6.3.9 Confirm discharge pressure of 68 to 74 psi.
6.3.10 Report "PS-17 pumping on generator" and the time to the Water Incident Lead.
6.4 Running on Generator Power

6.4.1 Record the pumping start time against the dispatch time. The planned hookup and start-up
      time is 150 min (Attachment A); report any overrun and its cause to Logistics.
6.4.2 Log fuel, load and discharge pressure every 4 h on F-WDS-207.
6.4.3 Request fuel at the threshold in WDS 03.322 section 6.3.
6.5 Return to Grid Supply

6.5.1 Return only on the Water Incident Lead's order, after Distribution Operations confirms
      FDR-AIK-2207 is stable.
6.5.2 Stop pump 2, then pump 1.
6.5.3 Move the MTS to OFF, then to UTILITY. Close CB-1.
6.5.4 Restart the pumps on grid power. Run the generator unloaded for 5 min, then stop it.
6.5.5 Leave the generator connected for 12 h if more weather is forecast.

This procedure sets how Logistics dispatches portable generators and delivers diesel to SGW
standby and portable generators during declared events.
2.0 SCOPE

Applies to water pump stations, lift stations, tanks with powered controls, and electric
facilities that run on generator power. Does not apply to customer-owned generators, including
hospital standby units such as GEN-HSP-TALLOWBRANCH.
3.0 RESPONSIBILITIES
Logistics Section Chief: owns the fuel plan, vendor call-outs and the generator dispatch log.

Fuel Coordinator (Logistics): receives F-MAL-022 requests, chooses the fuel source, tracks each
delivery to completion.

Water Incident Lead: sets generator priority among water facilities and requests portable
generators. Depot Supervisor, DEP-AIK-GRANITEVILLE: loads FTK-WREN-3 and readies
MGEN-HALBERD-500 for transport.
6.0 PROCEDURE
6.1 Requests
6.1.1 Generator dispatch and fuel requests are made on form F-MAL-022 and logged by Logistics.

6.1.2 The requester gives facility id, generator id, gauge reading, time of reading and load
      (kW).
6.1.3 Fuel Coordinator computes remaining run time from Attachment A.
6.2 Generator dispatch
6.2.1 Water Incident Lead confirms the target site and the connection point per WDS 03.318.
6.2.2 Depot Supervisor starts load-out and reports departure time to Logistics.
6.2.3 Logistics logs dispatched, on-site and running times against the F-MAL-022 number.
6.2.4 NOTE: Hookup and start-up times are set by WDS 03.318 section 6.4, not by this procedure.
6.3 Fuel source selection
6.3.1 Compare the vendor delivery time with the generator's remaining run time.

6.3.2 Where the vendor delivery time is longer than a generator's remaining run time, the SGW
      fuel truck is used first.

6.3.3 Call Altamaha for the next delivery to the same site at the same time, so the truck can be
      released.

6.3.4 Where two sites compete for FTK-WREN-3, the Water Incident Lead sets the order. Sites
      serving a hospital or critical facility per DOM 14.140 go first.
6.3.5 CAUTION: Do not fuel a running generator unless the unit is rated for hot refuelling.
6.4 Records of delivery
6.4.1 Driver records gallons delivered, gauge before and after, and time (24-hour EDT).
6.4.2 Vendor delivery tickets are scanned to the F-MAL-022 record within 12 h.

blocks: 4.0 DEFINITIONS

Flow-paced feed: metering pump speed set by a 4-20 mA signal from the station flow meter. Day
tank: the small tank feeding the metering pump directly.
5.0 PRECAUTIONS AND LIMITS

5.1 Hypochlorite metering pumps shall be on the generator-backed panel. Confirm this at each
    monthly test under WDS 03.350.

5.2 A metering pump that restarts before flow is established can overfeed. Never start feed with
    zero station flow.

5.3 Target free chlorine residual leaving the station is 1.2 to 2.0 mg/L. The distribution
    minimum is 0.2 mg/L in Georgia (Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. 391-3-5-.14); see WQC 07.140 for both
    states.

5.4 CAUTION: Hypochlorite off-gasses when heated. Keep the chemical room vent fan on the
    generator panel running.
5.5 Store no more than 30 days of hypochlorite at a station. It loses strength in summer heat.
6.0 PROCEDURE
6.1 On transfer to generator
6.1.1 Confirm pumps restarted and flow is above 150 gpm.
6.1.2 Confirm the metering pump is running and its stroke counter is moving.
6.1.3 Check the calibration column. Record the draw-down rate in gal/h.
6.1.4 Take a free chlorine reading at the station discharge tap within 30 min.
6.2 Flow-paced restart sequence
6.2.1 If feed did not restart, wait until station flow is stable for 2 min.
6.2.2 Start the metering pump in HAND at 25 percent speed.
6.2.3 After 5 min, switch to AUTO (flow-paced).
6.2.4 Recheck residual after 30 min.
6.3 While on generator power
6.3.1 Read the day tank level every 4 h with the generator readings.

6.3.2 Refill the day tank at 25 percent. Do not let it run dry; air in the suction line stops
      feed.
6.3.3 Take a residual at the discharge every 8 h and at the far zone point once per day.

6.3.4 If the discharge residual is below 1.0 mg/L, raise the feed rate by 10 percent and recheck
      in 30 min.

6.3.5 If any distribution reading is below the state minimum, notify the Water Compliance
      Officer.
6.4 On return to grid supply
6.4.1 Confirm feed restarted after retransfer.
6.4.2 Take a discharge residual within 30 min.
6.4.3 Log the end of generator operation in the feed log.

blocks: 1.0 PURPOSE

This procedure sets how the onsite standby generator at BPS-46 Tanyard Branch Booster is
started, loaded, watched and returned to standby when grid supply is lost.
2.0 SCOPE

Applies to BPS-46 Tanyard Branch Booster, Richmond district, Georgia. Does not apply to PS-17,
which has no onsite generator (see WDS 03.318).
3.0 RESPONSIBILITIES

3.1 Water Incident Lead: directs station start-up and shutdown during declared events; approves
    any manual transfer.

3.2 Station Operator (Richmond pump crew): performs the steps in section 6 and keeps the run
    log.

3.3 Water Control Room Operator: watches station status, zone pressure and tank level on SCADA;
    calls the Station Operator on any alarm.
3.4 Logistics Section Chief: arranges fuel on request under MAL 05.040.
6.0 PROCEDURE
6.1 Automatic start on loss of grid supply
6.1.1 Confirm on SCADA that the ATS transferred within 15 s of utility loss.
6.1.2 Confirm pumps 1 and 2 restarted on the lead-lag sequence. Allow 45 s stagger.
6.1.3 Log start time, kW and fuel level on F-WDS-207.

6.1.4 Notify the Water Incident Lead by phone. During business hours also notify the Richmond
      district supervisor.
6.1.5 Dispatch the Station Operator to site within 2 h to verify local readings.
6.2 Run-time monitoring

6.2.1 Read the fuel gauge and log kW, coolant temperature and oil pressure every 4 h on
      F-WDS-207.
6.2.2 Raise the refuel request at the tank level set in WDS 03.322. Use F-MAL-022.

6.2.3 Compare remaining run time against vendor delivery time. If remaining run time is shorter,
      ask Logistics for the SGW fuel truck first (MAL 05.040).
6.2.4 Record any alarm, shutdown or restart with the time in 24-hour format.
6.3 Failure of automatic transfer
NOTE: Use this subsection only on the Water Incident Lead's order.
6.3.1 Confirm the generator is running at rated voltage and frequency.
6.3.2 Place the ATS controller in OFF.
6.3.3 Operate the manual bypass handle to EMERGENCY. Observe the position flag.
6.3.4 Start pump 1 locally. Wait 60 s. Start pump 2.
6.3.5 Report the manual transfer to the Water Control Room Operator and log it.
6.4 Return to grid supply

blocks: 1.0 PURPOSE

This procedure sets how a portable bypass pump is placed and run when a sanitary lift station
cannot pump, so that the wet well does not overflow.
2.0 SCOPE

Applies to SGW wastewater lift stations in all SC and GA districts. Does not apply to treatment
plant influent pumping.
3.0 RESPONSIBILITIES

3.1 Water Incident Lead: orders bypass at any station during a declared event; sets the priority
    among stations when bypass pumps are short.
3.2 Collections Supervisor: places and runs the bypass; posts a watch.

3.3 Water Compliance Officer: decides whether an overflow is reportable and reports it per WQC
    07.150.
6.0 PROCEDURE
6.1 Assessment
6.1.1 Confirm the station alarm on SCADA. If SCADA is lost, follow WDS 03.115.
6.1.2 Determine the cause: grid outage, pump failure, control failure or flooding.
6.1.3 Read the time to overflow from Attachment A. Report it to the Water Incident Lead.
6.2 Bypass setup
6.2.1 Select a pump from Attachment B sized for the station's peak wet-weather flow.
6.2.2 Place the pump on level ground clear of traffic. Set cones and signs.

6.2.3 Run suction hose through the wet well hatch. Keep the foot valve at least 18 in. above the
      invert.

6.2.4 Connect discharge to the bypass connection on the force main. If none exists, discharge to
      the next downstream manhole.
6.2.5 Pressure test the discharge hose at operating pressure for 5 min. Inspect every joint.
6.2.6 Set the float controls: pump on at 60 percent, off at 25 percent.

6.2.7 Do a dry-run check: confirm the low-level float stops the pump before air enters the
      suction.
6.2.8 Start the pump. Confirm level falls.
6.3 Operation
6.3.1 Keep a person on watch at any bypass running without a level float.

6.3.2 Check fuel, hose joints and wet well level every 2 h. Log each check in the station log
      book.
6.3.3 Report any spill, however small, to the Water Compliance Officer at once.
6.4 Removal
6.4.1 Restore the station pumps and run two full cycles.

This template gives the wording and approval path for the public release of SGW's global
estimated time of restoration (ETR) during Event Types 1 to 3.
2.0 SCOPE

Applies to system-wide and district-level global ETR releases on sgw web outage pages, social
channels, media advisories and the IVR storm message. Does not apply to routine single-feeder
outages.
3.0 RULES FOR USE

3.1 The ETR Specialist (Planning Section) proposes the global ETR per DOM 14.206 section 6. The
    Incident Commander approves it before release.

3.2 The public release states the global ETR as a range (most customers restored between an
    earliest and a latest time), never as a single time. Take the earliest and latest bounds
    (the low and high ends of the restoration window) from the approved estimate per DOM 14.206
    section 6.

3.3 State the range per district when district estimates differ by more than 24 h. Otherwise use
    one system range.

3.4 Every release states the time of the next update. Use a clock time and date in EDT, not
    "later today".

3.5 Director, Corporate Communications, approves wording changes. Numbers come only from the
    approved Planning Section estimate.

3.6 Do not release a global ETR until the Incident Commander has approved the estimate. Damage
    assessment coverage rules are in DOM 14.206.
3.7 Releases shall go out within 30 min of Incident Commander approval.

1.0 PURPOSE

This procedure sets how SGW develops, approves, releases and revises estimated times of
restoration (ETRs) after a storm.
6.0 PROCEDURE
6.1 Before All-Clear
6.1.1 Run the pre-landfall model at each NHC advisory once the Event Type is 1 or 2.
6.1.2 Share the run with the Duty Manager for staffing decisions. Do not publish it.
6.2 Global ETR
6.2.1 Publish the global ETR within 24 h after the all-clear.

6.2.2 State the global ETR as a range: P25, P50 and P75 (range of the 25th, 50th and 75th
      percentiles).
6.2.3 The ETR Specialist proposes the global ETR on F-DOM-121 with the model inputs attached.

6.2.4 The Incident Commander and the Duty Manager approve the global ETR before release. Both
      signatures go on F-DOM-121.

6.2.5 Send the approved range to the Public Information Officer. Release wording follows PCN
      02.044.
NOTE: The P50 is the headline time in media statements. P25 and P75 are given as the range.
6.3 Regional ETRs

6.3.1 Regional ETRs follow once damage assessment has patrolled 80 percent of circuits in the
      region.

6.3.2 Use the patrol completion count from the Damage Assessment Coordinator, not crew
      estimates.
6.3.3 Approve and release regional ETRs as in 6.2.3 to 6.2.5.
6.4 Revision
6.4.1 Re-run the model at each operational period change.
6.4.2 Revise a published ETR when the P50 moves by more than 12 h.
6.4.3 A move of 12 h or less is logged but not released.
6.4.4 Revised ETRs need the same approvals as in 6.2.4.

    Rev E/1.

blocks: 1.0 PURPOSE

This procedure sets how SGW issues, announces and rescinds a boil water advisory (BWA) for its
Georgia water systems.
2.0 SCOPE

All SGW community water systems permitted by Georgia EPD, including the Richmond district. South
Carolina systems follow WQC 07.120. It does not cover advisories ordered directly by EPD; follow
the EPD order in that case.
3.0 RESPONSIBILITIES

Water Compliance Officer: owns the BWA decision with the Water Incident Lead. Notifies Georgia
EPD. Signs the rescission request.
Water Incident Lead: co-approves the public notice. Directs repair, flushing and isolation.

Director, Corporate Communications: releases the approved notice through the channels in
Attachment A.
Water Quality Technician: collects samples and fills in F-WQC-031.
6.0 PROCEDURE
6.1 Assessment
6.1.1 On a report from WDS 03.105 section 6.4, confirm the reading, time and location.
6.1.2 Issue a BWA when pressure falls below 20 psi or system integrity is lost.
6.1.3 Out of an abundance of caution, include adjoining streets on the same main.
6.1.4 Define the affected area by zone and street. Use the zone map in WQC 07.130.
6.2 Regulator Notification

6.2.1 Notify the Georgia EPD district inspector by phone before the public notice is released,
      where possible.

6.2.2 Nights and weekends, contact the Georgia State Emergency Operations Center. Ask that the
      EPD on-call be paged.
6.2.3 Record the name, time and number called on F-WQC-031.
6.2.4 Send the written notice copy to the district office within 24 h.
6.3 Public Notice
6.3.1 Prepare the notice from PCN 02.031.

6.3.2 The public notice is approved by the Water Incident Lead and the Water Compliance Officer.
      Both names and times go on F-WQC-031.

6.3.3 Communications releases the notice through the Attachment A channels within 2 h of the
      decision.

6.3.4 Phone critical customers in the area directly: hospitals, dialysis centres, nursing homes,
      schools.
6.3.5 Assign the notice serial BWA-GA-yymm-nn from the compliance log.
6.3.6 State the next update time in every notice.
6.4 Rescission
6.4.1 Rescission requires all of the following:
a. system integrity restored and positive pressure held;
b. the affected mains flushed per WDS 03.420;

blocks: 2.0 SCOPE

All SGW potable-water pressure zones in South Carolina and Georgia. It does not apply to
raw-water mains or to fire-line testing.
3.0 RESPONSIBILITIES
Water SCADA Operator: acknowledges pressure alarms and starts section 6.
Water Distribution Supervisor (on call): sends a crew to verify the reading in the field.
Water Incident Lead: directs station, tank and generator actions during an event.

Water Compliance Officer: decides, with the Water Incident Lead, whether a boil water advisory
or notice is issued.
6.0 PROCEDURE
6.1 Alarm
6.1.1 Acknowledge the alarm within 5 min.
6.1.2 Check station status, tank level and any active main break in the zone.
6.1.3 Trend the zone critical point for the past 2 h.
6.2 Field Verification
6.2.1 Send the on-call crew with a calibrated gauge.
6.2.2 Read at the hydrant nearest the critical point. Record the reading, time and hydrant id.
6.2.3 For zones fed by a booster on generator power, read at the station discharge too.
6.3 Restore Pressure
6.3.1 Start standby pumps if available.

6.3.2 If the station has lost power, follow WDS 03.322 (fixed generator) or WDS 03.318 (PS-17
      portable hookup).
6.3.3 Track tank drawdown per WDS 03.240.
6.3.4 Notify critical customers in the zone using DOM 14.140.
6.4 Below the State Minimum

6.4.1 When pressure at a service connection falls below the state minimum, notify the Water
      Compliance Officer within 1 h.

6.4.2 The Water Compliance Officer starts the boil water evaluation under WQC 07.114 (Georgia)
      or WQC 07.120 (South Carolina).

6.4.3 Record the affected streets and zones on the advisory map. Use the zone ids from
      Attachment A.
6.4.4 Keep reading the critical point every 30 min until pressure is above the minimum for 2 h.

CAUTION: Do not start flushing before the boil water decision is made. Flushing can pull
         pressure lower.
6.4.5 Hand the readings to the Water Compliance Officer for the regulator report.

blocks: 1.0 PURPOSE

This procedure sets how SGW records, reports and gives public notice of sanitary sewer overflows
(SSOs) in South Carolina and Georgia.
2.0 SCOPE

All SGW wastewater collection systems and lift stations. Plant bypasses are reported under the
plant's NPDES permit procedure.
3.0 RESPONSIBILITIES

3.1 Collections Supervisor: reports every overflow to the Water Compliance Officer as soon as
    found; estimates volume.

3.2 Water Compliance Officer: decides reportability, makes the agency reports and approves
    public notice.
3.3 Director, Corporate Communications: issues news releases when Attachment A requires one.
6.0 PROCEDURE
6.1 Field report

6.1.1 Note start time, location, cause and whether the overflow reached a stream, ditch or storm
      inlet.
6.1.2 Photograph the site.
6.1.3 Call the Water Compliance Officer. After hours, call the compliance on-call phone.
6.2 Volume
6.2.1 Estimate volume by Attachment B. Record the method.
6.2.2 Update the estimate when the overflow stops.
6.3 Agency reports
6.3.1 Report by phone or the agency portal within 24 h of becoming aware of the overflow.

6.3.2 South Carolina: report to SCDES Region staff; written report within 5 days (SC
      R.61-9.122.41(l)(6)).

6.3.3 Georgia: report to the Georgia EPD district office; follow Ga. Comp. R. & Regs.
      391-3-6-.05 for public notice and follow-up.
6.4 Public notice
6.4.1 Post signs at the overflow site and where the release entered state waters.

6.4.2 Where Attachment A requires it, notify the county health department and issue a news
      release within 24 h.

6.4.3 Georgia spills of 10,000 gal or more that reach state waters also need a legal notice in
      the county organ and stream monitoring. The Water Compliance Officer sets the monitoring
      points.
6.5 During declared storm events
6.5.1 Many overflows may occur during one event. Keep one SSO log per district.
6.5.2 With the agency's agreement, report overflows of one event once per day on the log.

6.5.3 Overflows that reach a drinking-water intake reach are reported at once regardless of
      batching.

The Water Incident Lead directs pump-station, tank and portable-generator actions for water
systems. The position reports to the Operations Section Chief and attends every IC briefing.
a. Orders portable-generator hookups per WDS 03.318.
b. Sets pump-station run priorities and tank fill targets.
c. Owns boil water advisory decisions jointly with the Water Compliance Officer.
3.8 Water Compliance Officer

The Water Compliance Officer owns boil water advisory decisions with the Water Incident Lead.
The officer is the SGW contact for state drinking-water regulators: SCDES in South Carolina and
Georgia EPD in Georgia.

plant's NPDES permit procedure.
3.0 RESPONSIBILITIES

3.1 Collections Supervisor: reports every overflow to the Water Compliance Officer as soon as
    found; estimates volume.

3.2 Water Compliance Officer: decides reportability, makes the agency reports and approves
    public notice.
3.3 Director, Corporate Communications: issues news releases when Attachment A requires one.
6.0 PROCEDURE
6.1 Field report

6.1.1 Note start time, location, cause and whether the overflow reached a stream, ditch or storm
      inlet.
6.1.2 Photograph the site.
6.1.3 Call the Water Compliance Officer. After hours, call the compliance on-call phone.
6.2 Volume
6.2.1 Estimate volume by Attachment B. Record the method.
6.2.2 Update the estimate when the overflow stops.
6.3 Agency reports
6.3.1 Report by phone or the agency portal within 24 h of becoming aware of the overflow.

6.3.2 South Carolina: report to SCDES Region staff; written report within 5 days (SC
      R.61-9.122.41(l)(6)).

6.3.3 Georgia: report to the Georgia EPD district office; follow Ga. Comp. R. & Regs.
      391-3-6-.05 for public notice and follow-up.
6.4 Public notice
6.4.1 Post signs at the overflow site and where the release entered state waters.

6.4.2 Where Attachment A requires it, notify the county health department and issue a news
      release within 24 h.

6.4.3 Georgia spills of 10,000 gal or more that reach state waters also need a legal notice in
      the county organ and stream monitoring. The Water Compliance Officer sets the monitoring
      points.
6.5 During declared storm events
6.5.1 Many overflows may occur during one event. Keep one SSO log per district.
6.5.2 With the agency's agreement, report overflows of one event once per day on the log.

6.5.3 Overflows that reach a drinking-water intake reach are reported at once regardless of
      batching.

blocks: 4.0 DEFINITIONS
Global ETR: the time by which 90 percent of affected customers are restored, system-wide.
Regional ETR: the same 90 percent measure for one operating region.
P25, P50, P75: the 25th, 50th and 75th percentiles of the modelled 90 percent restoration time.
All-clear: as defined in GEP 2H.01 section 3.0.
5.0 PRECAUTIONS AND LIMITS
5.1 Do not release an ETR that has not been approved per 6.2.4.
5.2 Model runs use crew counts on property or confirmed en route, not requested crews.
5.3 A model run older than 6 h shall not be used for release.
6.0 PROCEDURE
6.1 Before All-Clear
6.1.1 Run the pre-landfall model at each NHC advisory once the Event Type is 1 or 2.
6.1.2 Share the run with the Duty Manager for staffing decisions. Do not publish it.
6.2 Global ETR
6.2.1 Publish the global ETR within 24 h after the all-clear.

6.2.2 State the global ETR as a range: P25, P50 and P75 (range of the 25th, 50th and 75th
      percentiles).
6.2.3 The ETR Specialist proposes the global ETR on F-DOM-121 with the model inputs attached.

6.2.4 The Incident Commander and the Duty Manager approve the global ETR before release. Both
      signatures go on F-DOM-121.

6.2.5 Send the approved range to the Public Information Officer. Release wording follows PCN
      02.044.
NOTE: The P50 is the headline time in media statements. P25 and P75 are given as the range.
6.3 Regional ETRs

6.3.1 Regional ETRs follow once damage assessment has patrolled 80 percent of circuits in the
      region.

6.3.2 Use the patrol completion count from the Damage Assessment Coordinator, not crew
      estimates.
6.3.3 Approve and release regional ETRs as in 6.2.3 to 6.2.5.
6.4 Revision
6.4.1 Re-run the model at each operational period change.
6.4.2 Revise a published ETR when the P50 moves by more than 12 h.
6.4.3 A move of 12 h or less is logged but not released.
6.4.4 Revised ETRs need the same approvals as in 6.2.4.

This template gives the wording and approval path for the public release of SGW's global

Applies to system-wide and district-level global ETR releases on sgw web outage pages, social

    earliest and a latest time), never as a single time. Take the earliest and latest bounds

blocks: 4.0 DEMOBILIZATION
4.1 Trigger

The Planning Section Chief starts the Demobilization Plan when the remaining outage count has
fallen below

25 percent of the peak, or earlier when the IC directs. Release is never planned before the
global ETR has been published under DOM 14.206.
4.2 Release Order
Release resources in this order unless the IC directs otherwise:
a. Mutual-aid crews from the farthest home utility first.
b. Contract vegetation and line crews.
c. Mutual-aid crews from nearer utilities.
d. Native crews borrowed between districts.
e. Damage assessors, then wire guards.
4.3 Release Steps

4.3.1 The Duty Manager lists the crews that can be released, by district, at the planning
      meeting.

4.3.2 The Planning Section Chief adds them to the Demobilization Plan with a release date and
      time (EDT).
4.3.3 The IC approves the plan.

4.3.4 The Logistics Section Chief notifies SEE of mutual-aid releases through the channel used
      for the request (MAL 05.012).
4.3.5 Crews return SGW material, radios and badges at the yard. Check-out follows MAL 05.060.

4.3.6 The Safety Officer confirms each released crew has had the rest period in DOM 12.050
      before travel.

4.3.7 Logistics closes lodging and meal orders per MAL 05.030 within 24 h of the last crew
      leaving.

4.3.8 Logistics closes each staging yard when the last crew has left and the site is restored
      per MAL 05.020.

CAUTION: do not release a crew that holds a clearance or a Hot Line Hold. The clearance is
         returned under TSO
7.0 RECORDS
Demobilization Plan, release records, F-GEP-012, hot wash notes, AAR. Retain 7 years.

    years.

    expiry date. A bulletin overrides the named procedure section only until it expires.
